  keys); APEX keys are still the AOSP ones.
* Installer: `WSA-Next.exe` (see above) runs WSAPatch on Windows 11 build 28000+
  (`WsaClient.exe` fix for 26H1).
* Root for apps on `user` builds: AOSP has a root domain only on debug builds, so `0` needs a
  domain of its own there.
* Kernel migration: gradually move off Microsoft's aging `5.15.104` WSA kernel onto the current
  Microsoft Linux kernel baseline, porting and patching the WSA-specific pieces step by step so
  newer Android versions are no longer held back by a 2022 kernel.
* Android 18: parallel porting begins as soon as Android 18 lands in AOSP (potentially as early
  as February 2027), aiming for a working release by late summer 2027 with GPU/NPU acceleration,
  classic Bluetooth (RFCOMM), built-in laptop sensors, cameras, WWAN and native ARM64 builds.
* Bluetooth, which WSA never had, with the PC's own adapter (no USB passthrough or extra
  hardware): LE scanning, GATT and pairing work through the bridge in `WSA-Next.exe`, which
  implements the controller on top of the Windows Bluetooth APIs; classic Bluetooth (RFCOMM) is
  next. Microsoft's kernel stays: the Android Bluetooth stack runs in user space and needs no
  `CONFIG_BT`.
* MMS notices that arrive while Android is off (see *Telephony, the limits and edge cases*).
* Optional stable IP address for the Android side.

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/BoardConfig.mk`:

```mk
# WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
# Board configuration for Android 15 on the WSA 2407 host.

TARGET_ARCH := x86_64
TARGET_ARCH_VARIANT := x86_64
TARGET_CPU_ABI := x86_64
TARGET_2ND_ARCH := x86
TARGET_2ND_ARCH_VARIANT := x86_64
TARGET_2ND_CPU_ABI := x86

include build/make/target/board/BoardConfigMainlineCommon.mk

# WSA boots its own kernel and initrd; there is no bootloader or recovery.
TARGET_NO_KERNEL := true
TARGET_NO_BOOTLOADER := true
TARGET_NO_RECOVERY := true

# One plain ext4 image per WSA disk: no A/B, no super partition, no AVB
# (WSA's vendor fstab mounts the disks directly and verifies nothing).
AB_OTA_UPDATER := false
BOARD_AVB_ENABLE := false
BOARD_USES_SYSTEM_OTHER_ODEX :=

BOARD_SYSTEMIMAGE_FILE_SYSTEM_TYPE := ext4
BOARD_SYSTEM_EXTIMAGE_FILE_SYSTEM_TYPE := ext4
BOARD_PRODUCTIMAGE_FILE_SYSTEM_TYPE := ext4
BOARD_VENDORIMAGE_FILE_SYSTEM_TYPE := ext4

# Optional private WSA integration layer (SELinux additions for its services).
-include vendor/wsa/BoardConfigWsa.mk

# The Google Play variant copies Google's ARM64 translator (guest ARM64 ELF files,
# vendor/ndk_translation) into /system; they cannot be cc_prebuilt modules of this
# x86_64 build.
BUILD_BROKEN_ELF_PREBUILT_PRODUCT_COPY_FILES := true

# Images are sized to their content. BOARD_EXT4_SHARE_DUP_BLOCKS (inherited from
# BoardConfigMainlineCommon) deduplicates blocks, which keeps the download small and
# makes the images effectively read-only: every change goes through the build.

# Platform-side SELinux additions for the WSA host (properties used by patched vold).
SYSTEM_EXT_PRIVATE_SEPOLICY_DIRS += device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/sepolicy/system_ext/private

```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/bluetooth/Android.bp`:

```bp
// WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
// Bluetooth for WSA: an HCI HAL whose controller is the Bluetooth bridge on the Windows host
// (the PC's own adapter through WinRT), reached over a Hyper-V socket. The HAL publishes whether
// the bridge runs (sys.wsa.bluetooth.bridge); without it Android offers no Bluetooth.
//
// It lives in system_ext with a framework manifest fragment: the WSA vendor partition is
// reused unchanged. The Bluetooth stack prefers this AIDL HAL over the vendor's HIDL simulator
// (android.hardware.bluetooth@1.1-service.sim), which stays installed but unused.

package {
    default_applicable_licenses: ["Android-Apache-2.0"],
}

cc_binary {
    name: "android.hardware.bluetooth-service.wsa",
    relative_install_path: "hw",
    system_ext_specific: true,
    init_rc: ["android.hardware.bluetooth-service.wsa.rc"],
    vintf_fragments: ["android.hardware.bluetooth-service.wsa.xml"],
    srcs: [
        "BluetoothHci.cpp",
        "service.cpp",
    ],
    cflags: [
        "-Wall",
        "-Wextra",
        "-Werror",
    ],
    shared_libs: [
        "libbase",
        "libbinder_ndk",
        "libcutils",
        "libhidlbase",
        "liblog",
        "libutils",
    ],
    // Static: generic_system.mk allows no new libraries in /system, and the Bluetooth APEX
    // carries its own copy of the interface library.
    static_libs: [
        "android.hardware.bluetooth-V1-ndk",
        "android.hardware.bluetooth.hci",
    ],
}

```

```cpp
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.

#define LOG_TAG "android.hardware.bluetooth.service.wsa"

#include "BluetoothHci.h"

#include <android-base/properties.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/eventfd.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>  // before linux/vm_sockets.h, which needs struct sockaddr
#include <unistd.h>

#include <linux/vm_sockets.h>


#include "log/log.h"

using namespace ::android::hardware::bluetooth::hci;
using aidl::android::hardware::bluetooth::Status;

namespace aidl::android::hardware::bluetooth::impl {
namespace {

// Read by the WSA services in system_server (Bluetooth is offered only while it is "1").
constexpr char kBridgeProperty[] = "sys.wsa.bluetooth.bridge";

void PublishBridge(bool present) { ::android::base::SetProperty(kBridgeProperty, present ? "1" : "0"); }

}  // namespace

void OnDeath(void* cookie);

// Closes the HAL when the Bluetooth stack (the only client) dies, so that its restart can
// initialize again.
class BluetoothDeathRecipient {
 public:
  explicit BluetoothDeathRecipient(BluetoothHci* hci) : mHci(hci) {}

  void LinkToDeath(const std::shared_ptr<IBluetoothHciCallbacks>& cb) {
    mCb = cb;
    clientDeathRecipient_ = AIBinder_DeathRecipient_new(OnDeath);
    auto status = AIBinder_linkToDeath(mCb->asBinder().get(), clientDeathRecipient_, this /* cookie */);
    LOG_ALWAYS_FATAL_IF(status != STATUS_OK, "Unable to link to death recipient");
  }

  void serviceDied() {
    if (mCb != nullptr && !AIBinder_isAlive(mCb->asBinder().get())) {
      ALOGE("Bluetooth remote service has died");
    } else {
      ALOGE("BluetoothDeathRecipient::serviceDied called but service not dead");
      return;
    }
    {
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mHasDiedMutex);
      has_died_ = true;
    }
    mHci->close();
  }

  bool getHasDied() {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mHasDiedMutex);
    return has_died_;
  }

 private:
  BluetoothHci* mHci;
  std::shared_ptr<IBluetoothHciCallbacks> mCb;
  AIBinder_DeathRecipient* clientDeathRecipient_{nullptr};
  std::mutex mHasDiedMutex;
  bool has_died_{false};
};

void OnDeath(void* cookie) {
  static_cast<BluetoothDeathRecipient*>(cookie)->serviceDied();
}

BluetoothHci::BluetoothHci() {
  mDeathRecipient = std::make_shared<BluetoothDeathRecipient>(this);
  mWake = eventfd(0, EFD_CLOEXEC | EFD_NONBLOCK);
  PublishBridge(false);
  // The service lives as long as the process: this thread is never joined.
  std::thread(&BluetoothHci::serveBridge, this).detach();
}

void BluetoothHci::wake() {
  const uint64_t one = 1;
  (void)TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(write(mWake, &one, sizeof one));
}

void BluetoothHci::dropBridgeLocked() {
  if (mFd >= 0) {
    ::close(mFd);
    mFd = -1;
    ALOGI("The Windows Bluetooth bridge disconnected");
  }
  PublishBridge(false);
  mStateChanged.notify_all();
}

void BluetoothHci::serveBridge() {
  const int listener = socket(AF_VSOCK, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
  sockaddr_vm addr{};
  addr.svm_family = AF_VSOCK;
  addr.svm_cid = VMADDR_CID_ANY;
  addr.svm_port = kBridgePort;
  if (listener < 0 || bind(listener, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&addr), sizeof addr) != 0 || listen(listener, 1) != 0) {
    ALOGE("Cannot listen on vsock port 0x%08x: %s", kBridgePort, strerror(errno));
    return;
  }
  for (;;) {
    pollfd fds[3] = {};
    fds[0].fd = listener;
    fds[0].events = POLLIN;
    fds[1].fd = mWake;
    fds[1].events = POLLIN;
    nfds_t count = 2;
    int idle = -1;
    {
      // While the stack uses the connection, its reader watches it; idle, this thread does.
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
      if (mFd >= 0 && mState == HalState::READY) idle = mFd;
    }
    if (idle >= 0) {
      fds[2].fd = idle;
      fds[2].events = POLLIN | POLLRDHUP;
      count = 3;
    }
    if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(fds, count, -1)) < 0) continue;

    if (fds[1].revents & POLLIN) {
      uint64_t value = 0;
      (void)TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(read(mWake, &value, sizeof value));
    }
    if (fds[0].revents & POLLIN) {
      const int fd = accept4(listener, nullptr, nullptr, SOCK_CLOEXEC);
      if (fd >= 0) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
        if (mState == HalState::READY) {
          if (mFd >= 0) ::close(mFd);  // a new bridge replaces a stale connection
          mFd = fd;
          mBridgeLost = false;
          ALOGI("The Windows Bluetooth bridge connected");
          PublishBridge(true);
          mStateChanged.notify_all();
        } else {
          // The stack still talks to the previous connection: switch when it lets go.
          if (mPendingFd >= 0) ::close(mPendingFd);
          mPendingFd = fd;
        }
      }
    }
    if (count == 3 && fds[2].revents) {
      // Idle: the bridge went away, or sent a leftover (the answer to the reset of close()).
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
      if (mFd == idle && mState == HalState::READY) {
        char buffer[512];
        if ((fds[2].revents & (POLLHUP | POLLRDHUP | POLLERR)) || read(idle, buffer, sizeof buffer) <= 0) dropBridgeLocked();
      }
    }
  }
}

void BluetoothHci::readerLoop(int fd) {
  pollfd fds[2] = {};
  fds[0].fd = fd;
  fds[0].events = POLLIN;
  fds[1].fd = mReaderStop;
  fds[1].events = POLLIN;
  for (;;) {
    if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(fds, 2, -1)) < 0) return;
    if (fds[1].revents) return;  // stopReader()
    if (fds[0].revents & POLLIN) mH4->OnDataReady();
    if (fds[0].revents & (POLLHUP | POLLERR)) {
      mH4->OnDataReady();  // lets H4Protocol see the end and report the disconnection
      return;
    }
    if (mBridgeLost) return;
  }
}

void BluetoothHci::stopReader() {
  if (mReaderStop >= 0) {
    const uint64_t one = 1;
    (void)TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(write(mReaderStop, &one, sizeof one));
  }
  if (mReader.joinable()) mReader.join();
  if (mReaderStop >= 0) {
    ::close(mReaderStop);
    mReaderStop = -1;
  }
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus BluetoothHci::initialize(const std::shared_ptr<IBluetoothHciCallbacks>& cb) {
  ALOGI(__func__);
  if (cb == nullptr) {
    ALOGE("cb == nullptr! -> Unable to call initializationComplete(ERR)");
    return ndk::ScopedAStatus::fromServiceSpecificError(STATUS_BAD_VALUE);
  }

  std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mStateMutex);
  if (mState != HalState::READY) {
    const HalState old_state = mState;
    lock.unlock();
    ALOGE("initialize: Unexpected State %d", static_cast<int>(old_state));
    close();
    cb->initializationComplete(Status::ALREADY_INITIALIZED);
    return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
  }
  // system_server offers Bluetooth only while a bridge is connected; this is the race of a
  // bridge that left just now.
  if (mFd < 0) {
    lock.unlock();
    ALOGE("No Windows Bluetooth bridge is connected (vsock port 0x%08x)", kBridgePort);
    cb->initializationComplete(Status::UNABLE_TO_OPEN_INTERFACE);
    return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
  }
  mState = HalState::INITIALIZING;
  const int fd = mFd;
  lock.unlock();

  mCb = cb;
  mDeathRecipient->LinkToDeath(mCb);
  mH4 = std::make_shared<H4Protocol>(
      fd,
      [](const std::vector<uint8_t>& /* raw_command */) {
        ALOGE("The bridge sent a command packet; dropped");
      },
      [this](const std::vector<uint8_t>& raw_acl) { mCb->aclDataReceived(raw_acl); },
      [this](const std::vector<uint8_t>& raw_sco) { mCb->scoDataReceived(raw_sco); },
      [this](const std::vector<uint8_t>& raw_event) { mCb->hciEventReceived(raw_event); },
      [this](const std::vector<uint8_t>& raw_iso) { mCb->isoDataReceived(raw_iso); },
      [this]() {
        // The stack notices the missing controller through its command timeout; the published
        // absence makes system_server turn Bluetooth off, and close() releases the connection.
        ALOGE("The Windows Bluetooth bridge disconnected");
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
        mBridgeLost = true;
        PublishBridge(false);
      });
  mReaderStop = eventfd(0, EFD_CLOEXEC);
  mReader = std::thread(&BluetoothHci::readerLoop, this, fd);

  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
    mState = HalState::ONE_CLIENT;
  }
  mStateChanged.notify_all();
  wake();  // the connection is the reader's now
  ALOGI("initialization complete");
  auto status = mCb->initializationComplete(Status::SUCCESS);
  if (!status.isOk()) {
    if (!mDeathRecipient->getHasDied()) {
      ALOGE("Error sending init callback, but no death notification");
    }
    close();
    return ndk::ScopedAStatus::fromServiceSpecificError(STATUS_FAILED_TRANSACTION);
  }
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus BluetoothHci::close() {
  ALOGI(__func__);
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
    if (mState != HalState::ONE_CLIENT) {
      LOG_ALWAYS_FATAL_IF(mState == HalState::INITIALIZING, "mState is INITIALIZING");
      ALOGI("Already closed");
      return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
    }
    mState = HalState::CLOSING;
  }

  stopReader();

  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
    if (mBridgeLost) {
      dropBridgeLocked();
      mBridgeLost = false;
    } else if (mFd >= 0) {
      // The stack is gone: a reset ends the bridge's scanning and connections.
      const uint8_t reset[] = {0x01, 0x03, 0x0c, 0x00};
      if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(write(mFd, reset, sizeof reset)) != static_cast<ssize_t>(sizeof reset)) dropBridgeLocked();
    }
    if (mPendingFd >= 0) {
      // A bridge connected again while the stack used the old connection: take the new one.
      if (mFd >= 0) ::close(mFd);
      mFd = mPendingFd;
      mPendingFd = -1;
      PublishBridge(true);
    }
    mState = HalState::READY;
    mH4 = nullptr;
  }
  mStateChanged.notify_all();
  wake();  // idle again: serveBridge watches the connection
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus BluetoothHci::sendHciCommand(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) {
  return send(PacketType::COMMAND, packet);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus BluetoothHci::sendAclData(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) {
  return send(PacketType::ACL_DATA, packet);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus BluetoothHci::sendScoData(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) {
  return send(PacketType::SCO_DATA, packet);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus BluetoothHci::sendIsoData(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) {
  return send(PacketType::ISO_DATA, packet);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus BluetoothHci::send(PacketType type, const std::vector<uint8_t>& v) {
  if (v.empty()) {
    ALOGE("Packet is empty, no data was found to be sent");
    return ndk::ScopedAStatus::fromExceptionCode(EX_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT);
  }
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mStateMutex);
  if (mH4 == nullptr || mFd < 0) {
    return ndk::ScopedAStatus::fromExceptionCode(EX_ILLEGAL_STATE);
  }
  mH4->Send(type, v);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

}  // namespace aidl::android::hardware::bluetooth::impl
```

```h
// Bluetooth HCI HAL for WSA. Based on hardware/interfaces/bluetooth/aidl/default; the
// controller is not a UART but the Bluetooth bridge on the Windows host, which connects to this
// HAL over a Hyper-V socket (vsock port "WSBT") when it starts. HCI packets travel in H4 framing
// (one packet type byte, then the packet) in both directions.
//
// Everything is event driven: one thread waits (poll, no timeout) for the bridge to connect, for
// an idle connection to end and for state changes (eventfd); while the Bluetooth stack uses the
// HAL, a reader thread waits on the connection. The HAL publishes whether a bridge is connected
// in sys.wsa.bluetooth.bridge ("1" / "0"); the WSA services in system_server turn that into the
// no_bluetooth user restriction, so without the bridge Android offers no Bluetooth at all
// instead of a stack that cannot start.

#pragma once

#include <aidl/android/hardware/bluetooth/BnBluetoothHci.h>
#include <aidl/android/hardware/bluetooth/IBluetoothHciCallbacks.h>

#include <atomic>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>

#include "h4_protocol.h"

namespace aidl::android::hardware::bluetooth::impl {

class BluetoothDeathRecipient;

class BluetoothHci : public BnBluetoothHci {
 public:
  // vsock port of the HAL: "WSBT" (the Windows bridge connects to it).
  static constexpr unsigned int kBridgePort = 0x57534254;

  BluetoothHci();

  ndk::ScopedAStatus initialize(const std::shared_ptr<IBluetoothHciCallbacks>& cb) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus sendHciCommand(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus sendAclData(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus sendScoData(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus sendIsoData(const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus close() override;

 private:
  // Accepts bridge connections and watches an idle one; never returns.
  void serveBridge();
  // Makes serveBridge look at the state again (eventfd).
  void wake();
  // The connection is gone (call with mStateMutex held).
  void dropBridgeLocked();
  // Reads the bridge connection into mH4 while the stack uses it, until stopReader().
  void readerLoop(int fd);
  void stopReader();

  [[nodiscard]] ndk::ScopedAStatus send(::android::hardware::bluetooth::hci::PacketType type,
                                        const std::vector<uint8_t>& packet);

  int mFd{-1};         // the bridge connection, -1 while there is none
  int mPendingFd{-1};  // a new connection that arrived while the stack still used the old one
  int mWake{-1};       // eventfd for serveBridge
  std::shared_ptr<IBluetoothHciCallbacks> mCb;
  std::shared_ptr<::android::hardware::bluetooth::hci::H4Protocol> mH4;
  std::shared_ptr<BluetoothDeathRecipient> mDeathRecipient;
  std::thread mReader;
  int mReaderStop{-1};      // eventfd that ends readerLoop
  // The reader saw the bridge go; the fd is closed when the stack lets go. Atomic: the reader
  // checks it without mStateMutex, which a send() blocked in write() may hold - the reader must
  // keep draining the connection then, or both sides could wait for each other.
  std::atomic<bool> mBridgeLost{false};
  std::condition_variable mStateChanged;

  // Don't close twice or open before close is complete.
  std::mutex mStateMutex;
  enum class HalState {
    READY,
    INITIALIZING,
    ONE_CLIENT,
    CLOSING,
  } mState{HalState::READY};
};

}  // namespace aidl::android::hardware::bluetooth::impl
```

```cpp
#define LOG_TAG "android.hardware.bluetooth.service.wsa"

#include <android/binder_manager.h>
#include <android/binder_process.h>

#include "BluetoothHci.h"
#include "log/log.h"

using ::aidl::android::hardware::bluetooth::impl::BluetoothHci;

int main(int /* argc */, char** /* argv */) {
  ALOGI("Bluetooth HAL starting");
  if (!ABinderProcess_setThreadPoolMaxThreadCount(0)) {
    ALOGE("failed to set thread pool max thread count");
    return 1;
  }
  std::shared_ptr<BluetoothHci> service = ndk::SharedRefBase::make<BluetoothHci>();
  const std::string instance = std::string() + BluetoothHci::descriptor + "/default";
  if (AServiceManager_addService(service->asBinder().get(), instance.c_str()) != STATUS_OK) {
    ALOGE("Could not register as a service!");
    return 1;
  }
  ABinderProcess_joinThreadPool();
  return 0;
}
```

```bp
// WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
// Root for apps, every request confirmed on Windows with Windows Hello (the elevation bridge of
// WSA-Next.exe, vsock port "WSEV"). Instead of Magisk-style root: the images stay as built and
// signed, SELinux stays enforcing, nothing has to be hidden from apps, and nothing is rooted
// until the user turns it on in WSA-Next.
//
//   0                  what apps run - root is uid 0 ("0", "0 -c 'command'", "0 program args")
//   wsa-elevated       the daemon that asks Windows (init service, socket /dev/socket/wsa_elevate)
//   wsa-elevate-exec   started by the daemon only; its executable enters the elevated domain
//
// Installed on userdebug builds (PRODUCT_PACKAGES_DEBUG): the elevated domain exists only there.

package {
    default_applicable_licenses: ["Android-Apache-2.0"],
}

cc_defaults {
    name: "wsa_elevate_defaults",
    system_ext_specific: true,
    cflags: [
        "-Wall",
        "-Wextra",
        "-Werror",
    ],
}

cc_binary {
    name: "wsa-elevated",
    defaults: ["wsa_elevate_defaults"],
    init_rc: ["wsa-elevated.rc"],
    srcs: ["elevated.cpp"],
    shared_libs: [
        "libcutils",
        "liblog",
    ],
}

cc_binary {
    name: "wsa-zero",
    stem: "0",
    defaults: ["wsa_elevate_defaults"],
    srcs: ["zero.cpp"],
    // 0 replaces AOSP's debug su (/system/xbin/su, usable by adb shell only): no su binary in the
    // image, nothing for root checks to find. "adb root" does not need it.
    overrides: ["su"],
}

cc_binary {
    name: "wsa-elevate-exec",
    defaults: ["wsa_elevate_defaults"],
    srcs: ["exec.cpp"],
}
```

```cpp
/*
 * Copyright 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
 *
 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
 * You may obtain a copy of the License at
 *
 *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.

// wsa-elevated: decides nothing itself. It asks the elevation bridge of WSA-Next.exe on Windows
// (vsock port "WSEV"), which shows Windows Hello with the app and the command, and starts the
// command as root only on a verified answer. Without the bridge (root for Android apps turned
// off on Windows) every request is refused. All waits are on file descriptors, without timeouts.
#define LOG_TAG "wsa-elevated"

#include <cutils/sockets.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/eventfd.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>  // before linux/vm_sockets.h, which needs struct sockaddr
#include <sys/syscall.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <linux/vm_sockets.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <fstream>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <sstream>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include "log/log.h"
#include "protocol.h"

namespace wsa::elevate {
namespace {

// Host protocol (src/biometrics/ElevationProtocol.h on Windows).
constexpr uint32_t kBridgePort = 0x57534556;        // "WSEV"
constexpr uint32_t kHostMagic = 0x56455357;         // 'W','S','E','V'
constexpr uint8_t kOpRequest = 1, kOpAnswer = 2, kOpCancel = 3, kOpConfig = 4;
constexpr uint8_t kGrantedStatus = 1, kDeniedStatus = 2, kNoHelloStatus = 3, kBusyStatus = 4;
constexpr uint8_t kNoBridge = 0xFF;  // local: no bridge connected, or it went away
constexpr size_t kMaxShown = 1024;   // of the command sent to Windows
constexpr char kSuLink[] = "/dev/wsa/bin/su";  // on everyone's PATH (wsa-elevated.rc)
constexpr char kZero[] = "/system_ext/bin/0";

// "su for root apps": the link exists exactly while a bridge that wants it is connected.
void SetSuLink(bool present) {
  if (present) {
    if (symlink(kZero, kSuLink) == 0) ALOGI("su for root apps: on");
    else if (errno != EEXIST) ALOGE("Cannot create %s: %s", kSuLink, strerror(errno));
  } else if (unlink(kSuLink) == 0) {
    ALOGI("su for root apps: off");
  }
}

struct HostFrame {
  uint32_t magic = kHostMagic;
  uint8_t op = 0;
  uint8_t status = 0;
  uint16_t payloadLen = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(HostFrame) == 8);

bool SendAll(int fd, const void* data, size_t size) {
  const auto* p = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(data);
  while (size) {
    const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(send(fd, p, size, MSG_NOSIGNAL));
    if (n <= 0) return false;
    p += n;
    size -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
  }
  return true;
}

bool RecvAll(int fd, void* data, size_t size) {
  auto* p = static_cast<uint8_t*>(data);
  while (size) {
    const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(recv(fd, p, size, 0));
    if (n <= 0) return false;
    p += n;
    size -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
  }
  return true;
}

void PutU32(std::string& out, uint32_t v) {
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) out += static_cast<char>((v >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF);
}

void PutText(std::string& out, const std::string& text) {
  const size_t n = std::min<size_t>(text.size(), kMaxShown);
  out += static_cast<char>(n & 0xFF);
  out += static_cast<char>(n >> 8);
  out.append(text, 0, n);
}

// The connection from the elevation bridge, and the one request it is deciding.
class HostLink {
 public:
  HostLink() : mAnswerEvent(eventfd(0, EFD_CLOEXEC | EFD_NONBLOCK)) {}

  void Start() { std::thread(&HostLink::Serve, this).detach(); }

  // Asks Windows. While waiting, a client that goes away cancels the dialog.
  uint8_t Ask(uint32_t uid, const std::string& packages, const std::string& command, int client) {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> one(mAskLock);  // one dialog at a time
    uint32_t id = 0;
    {
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
      if (mConnection < 0) return kNoBridge;
      id = ++mNextId;
      mPending = id;
      mAnswer.reset();
      uint64_t drain = 0;
      (void)TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(read(mAnswerEvent, &drain, sizeof drain));  // a late answer of an earlier request
      std::string payload;
      PutU32(payload, id);
      PutU32(payload, uid);
      PutText(payload, packages);
      PutText(payload, command);
      const HostFrame frame{kHostMagic, kOpRequest, 0, static_cast<uint16_t>(payload.size())};
      if (!SendAll(mConnection, &frame, sizeof frame) || !SendAll(mConnection, payload.data(), payload.size())) {
        mPending = 0;
        return kNoBridge;
      }
    }
    bool canceled = false;
    for (;;) {
      pollfd fds[2] = {{mAnswerEvent, POLLIN, 0}, {canceled ? -1 : client, POLLRDHUP, 0}};
      if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(fds, 2, -1)) < 0) return kNoBridge;
      if (fds[0].revents & POLLIN) break;
      if (fds[1].revents) {
        canceled = true;  // the client gave up: close the dialog, its answer still ends the wait
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
        std::string payload;
        PutU32(payload, id);
        const HostFrame frame{kHostMagic, kOpCancel, 0, static_cast<uint16_t>(payload.size())};
        if (mConnection >= 0) (void)(SendAll(mConnection, &frame, sizeof frame) && SendAll(mConnection, payload.data(), payload.size()));
      }
    }
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    mPending = 0;
    return canceled ? kDeniedStatus : mAnswer.value_or(kNoBridge);
  }

 private:
  void AnswerLocked(uint8_t status) {
    mAnswer = status;
    const uint64_t one = 1;
    (void)TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(write(mAnswerEvent, &one, sizeof one));
  }

  void DropLocked() {
    if (mConnection >= 0) ::close(mConnection);
    mConnection = -1;
    SetSuLink(false);
    if (mPending) AnswerLocked(kNoBridge);
  }

  void Serve() {
    const int listener = socket(AF_VSOCK, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
    sockaddr_vm addr{};
    addr.svm_family = AF_VSOCK;
    addr.svm_cid = VMADDR_CID_ANY;
    addr.svm_port = kBridgePort;
    if (listener < 0 || bind(listener, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&addr), sizeof addr) != 0 || listen(listener, 1) != 0) {
      ALOGE("Cannot listen on vsock port 0x%08x: %s", kBridgePort, strerror(errno));
      return;
    }
    for (;;) {
      int connection = -1;
      {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
        connection = mConnection;
      }
      pollfd fds[2] = {{listener, POLLIN, 0}, {connection, POLLIN | POLLRDHUP, 0}};
      if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(fds, 2, -1)) < 0) continue;
      if (fds[0].revents & POLLIN) {
        const int fd = accept4(listener, nullptr, nullptr, SOCK_CLOEXEC);
        if (fd >= 0) {
          std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
          DropLocked();  // a new bridge replaces the previous connection
          mConnection = fd;
          ALOGI("The elevation bridge connected");
        }
        continue;
      }
      if (connection < 0 || fds[1].revents == 0) continue;
      HostFrame frame{};
      uint8_t body[4] = {};
      // Data first: a last frame may come with the hangup (read until recv says the end).
      bool ok = (fds[1].revents & POLLIN) && RecvAll(connection, &frame, sizeof frame) && frame.magic == kHostMagic &&
                frame.payloadLen <= 64;
      for (uint16_t i = 0; ok && i < frame.payloadLen; ++i) {
        uint8_t byte = 0;
        ok = RecvAll(connection, &byte, 1);
        if (i < 4) body[i] = byte;
      }
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
      if (connection != mConnection) continue;
      if (!ok) {
        ALOGI("The elevation bridge disconnected");
        DropLocked();
        continue;
      }
      const uint32_t id = body[0] | (body[1] << 8) | (body[2] << 16) | (static_cast<uint32_t>(body[3]) << 24);
      if (frame.op == kOpAnswer && frame.payloadLen >= 4 && mPending && id == mPending) AnswerLocked(frame.status);
      else if (frame.op == kOpConfig) SetSuLink(frame.status == 1);
    }
  }

  std::mutex mAskLock, mLock;
  int mConnection = -1;
  const int mAnswerEvent;
  uint32_t mNextId = 0, mPending = 0;
  std::optional<uint8_t> mAnswer;
};

HostLink& Host() {
  static HostLink* link = new HostLink();  // lives as long as the daemon
  return *link;
}

// The always-on link to WSA-Next on Windows for Google Play registration (vsock "WSRG",
// protocol.h): the host connects whenever it runs, whether root for apps is on or not.
class RegistrationLink {
 public:
  void Start() { std::thread(&RegistrationLink::Serve, this).detach(); }

  // Hands the device ID to the host; its one-byte answer, or kUnavailable without a host.
  uint8_t Offer(const std::string& id) {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    if (mConnection < 0) return kUnavailable;
    std::string message = "RGID";
    message += static_cast<char>(id.size());
    message += id;
    uint8_t reply = 0;
    if (!SendAll(mConnection, message.data(), message.size()) || !RecvAll(mConnection, &reply, 1)) {
      ::close(mConnection);
      mConnection = -1;
      return kUnavailable;
    }
    return reply;
  }

 private:
  void Serve() {
    const int listener = socket(AF_VSOCK, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
    sockaddr_vm addr{};
    addr.svm_family = AF_VSOCK;
    addr.svm_cid = VMADDR_CID_ANY;
    addr.svm_port = kRegistrationPort;
    if (listener < 0 || bind(listener, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&addr), sizeof addr) != 0 || listen(listener, 1) != 0) {
      ALOGE("Cannot listen on registration vsock port 0x%08x: %s", kRegistrationPort, strerror(errno));
      return;
    }
    for (;;) {
      const int fd = accept4(listener, nullptr, nullptr, SOCK_CLOEXEC);
      if (fd < 0) continue;
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
      if (mConnection >= 0) ::close(mConnection);
      mConnection = fd;
      ALOGI("The registration helper connected");
    }
  }

  std::mutex mLock;
  int mConnection = -1;
};

RegistrationLink& RegistrationHost() {
  static RegistrationLink* link = new RegistrationLink();
  return *link;
}

// The packages of an app uid ("com.termux"; several for a shared uid), from packages.list.
std::string Packages(uid_t uid) {
  if (uid == 0) return "root";
  if (uid == 2000) return "shell";
  const uid_t appId = uid % 100000;
  std::ifstream list("/data/system/packages.list");
  std::string line, found;
  while (std::getline(list, line)) {
    std::istringstream fields(line);
    std::string name;
    uid_t id = 0;
    if (!(fields >> name >> id) || id != appId) continue;
    found += (found.empty() ? "" : ",") + name;
  }
  return found;
}

// The command as the user will read it on Windows.
std::string Shown(const std::vector<std::string>& argv) {
  std::string out;
  for (const std::string& arg : argv) {
    if (!out.empty()) out += ' ';
    const bool quote = arg.empty() || arg.find_first_of(" \t\"'\\$`") != std::string::npos;
    if (!quote) {
      out += arg;
      continue;
    }
    out += '\'';
    for (const char c : arg) out += c == '\'' ? std::string("'\\''") : std::string(1, c);
    out += '\'';
  }
  return out;
}

std::string EnvValue(const std::vector<std::string>& env, const std::string& name) {
  for (const std::string& entry : env)
    if (entry.size() > name.size() && entry.compare(0, name.size(), name) == 0 && entry[name.size()] == '=') return entry.substr(name.size() + 1);
  return {};
}

// A program name as the client's shell would find it: absolute, relative to cwd, or on its PATH.
std::string Resolve(const std::string& program, const std::vector<std::string>& env, const std::string& cwd) {
  if (program.find('/') != std::string::npos) return program[0] == '/' ? program : cwd + "/" + program;
  std::string path = EnvValue(env, "PATH");
  if (path.empty()) path = "/product/bin:/apex/com.android.runtime/bin:/apex/com.android.art/bin:/system_ext/bin:/system/bin:/system/xbin:/odm/bin:/vendor/bin:/vendor/xbin";
  std::istringstream dirs(path);
  std::string dir;
  while (std::getline(dirs, dir, ':')) {
    if (dir.empty()) continue;
    const std::string candidate = dir + "/" + program;
    if (access(candidate.c_str(), X_OK) == 0) return candidate;
  }
  return "/system/bin/" + program;
}

struct ClientRequest {
  Request header;
  std::string cwd;
  std::vector<std::string> argv, env;
};

// The rest of a request whose first field (the magic) the caller has read.
std::optional<ClientRequest> ReadRequest(int fd, uint32_t magic) {
  ClientRequest r;
  r.header.magic = magic;
  static_assert(offsetof(Request, magic) == 0);
  if (!RecvAll(fd, reinterpret_cast<uint8_t*>(&r.header) + sizeof magic, sizeof r.header - sizeof magic)) return std::nullopt;
  const Request& h = r.header;
  if (h.magic != kRequestMagic || h.version != kVersion || h.length > kMaxStrings || h.argc > kMaxCount || h.envc > kMaxCount)
    return std::nullopt;
  for (const int32_t f : h.fds)
    if (f < 0) return std::nullopt;
  std::string strings(h.length, '\0');
  if (h.length && !RecvAll(fd, strings.data(), strings.size())) return std::nullopt;
  std::vector<std::string> parts;
  size_t start = 0;
  while (start < strings.size()) {
    const size_t end = strings.find('\0', start);
    if (end == std::string::npos) return std::nullopt;
    parts.emplace_back(strings, start, end - start);
    start = end + 1;
  }
  if (parts.size() != 1 + h.argc + h.envc) return std::nullopt;
  r.cwd = parts[0].empty() ? "/" : parts[0];
  r.argv.assign(parts.begin() + 1, parts.begin() + 1 + h.argc);
  r.env.assign(parts.begin() + 1 + h.argc, parts.end());
  return r;
}

void SendReply(int fd, uint8_t code) { (void)SendAll(fd, &code, 1); }

// The Google Services Framework ID (decimal), or empty before Play services have checked in.
// It lives in Play services' own data (shared_prefs/Checkin.xml), which this narrow domain
// cannot read: the launcher reads it in the elevated domain and prints nothing but the number.
std::string ReadGsfId() {
  int out[2];
  if (pipe2(out, O_CLOEXEC) != 0) return {};
  const pid_t child = fork();
  if (child == 0) {
    if (dup2(out[1], 1) < 0) _exit(126);  // dup2 clears close-on-exec
    syscall(__NR_close_range, 3, ~0U, 0);
    char launcher[] = "wsa-elevate-exec", option[sizeof kGsfIdOption];
    memcpy(option, kGsfIdOption, sizeof option);
    char* argv[] = {launcher, option, nullptr};
    char* envp[] = {nullptr};
    execve(kLauncher, argv, envp);
    _exit(127);
  }
  close(out[1]);
  std::string id;
  char buffer[32];
  ssize_t n = 0;
  while (id.size() <= 20 && (n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(read(out[0], buffer, sizeof buffer))) > 0) id.append(buffer, static_cast<size_t>(n));
  close(out[0]);
  int status = 0;
  const bool exited = child > 0 && TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(waitpid(child, &status, 0)) == child && WIFEXITED(status) && WEXITSTATUS(status) == 0;
  if (!exited || id.empty() || id.size() > 20 || id.find_first_not_of("0123456789") != std::string::npos) return {};
  return id;  // empty above: Play services have not checked in yet, or there are none
}

// Only the registration app may have the ID or offer it on Windows (protocol.h).
bool FromRegistrationApp(int client, uid_t uid, const char* what) {
  if (Packages(uid) == kRegistrationPackage) return true;
  ALOGW("uid %u asked to %s: refused (only %s may)", uid, what, kRegistrationPackage);
  SendReply(client, kDenied);
  return false;
}

void ServeGsfId(int client, uid_t uid) {
  if (!FromRegistrationApp(client, uid, "read the device ID")) return;
  const std::string id = ReadGsfId();
  if (id.empty()) {
    SendReply(client, kFailed);
    return;
  }
  std::string reply(1, static_cast<char>(kGranted));
  reply += static_cast<char>(id.size());
  reply += id;
  (void)SendAll(client, reply.data(), reply.size());
}

void ServeRegisterOnWindows(int client, uid_t uid) {
  if (!FromRegistrationApp(client, uid, "offer the registration on Windows")) return;
  const std::string id = ReadGsfId();
  SendReply(client, id.empty() ? kFailed : RegistrationHost().Offer(id));
}

void Serve(int client) {
  ucred peer{};
  socklen_t size = sizeof peer;
  if (getsockopt(client, SOL_SOCKET, SO_PEERCRED, &peer, &size) != 0) return;
  uint32_t magic = 0;
  if (!RecvAll(client, &magic, sizeof magic)) return;
  if (magic == kGsfIdMagic) {
    ServeGsfId(client, peer.uid);
    return;
  }
  if (magic == kRegisterOnWindowsMagic) {
    ServeRegisterOnWindows(client, peer.uid);
    return;
  }
  // A reference to exactly this client process (its pid cannot be reused while held).
  const int pidfd = static_cast<int>(syscall(__NR_pidfd_open, peer.pid, 0));
  if (pidfd < 0) return;
  const auto request = ReadRequest(client, magic);
  if (!request) {
    SendReply(client, kInvalid);
    close(pidfd);
    return;
  }
  // The pid was the client's when it connected; its socket still open means it still is.
  pollfd alive{client, POLLRDHUP, 0};
  if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(&alive, 1, 0)) != 0) {
    close(pidfd);
    return;
  }

  const std::string packages = Packages(peer.uid);
  const std::string shown = request->argv.empty() ? std::string() : Shown(request->argv);
  ALOGI("uid %u (%s) asks for root: %s", peer.uid, packages.empty() ? "?" : packages.c_str(), shown.empty() ? "<interactive shell>" : shown.c_str());
  // A process that is root in the elevated domain already gains nothing: no second question.
  // Its context comes from the kernel (SO_PEERSEC), like its uid.
  char context[256] = {};
  socklen_t contextSize = sizeof context - 1;
  const bool elevated = peer.uid == 0 && getsockopt(client, SOL_SOCKET, SO_PEERSEC, context, &contextSize) == 0 &&
                        strncmp(context, "u:r:su:", 7) == 0;
  const uint8_t answer = elevated ? kGrantedStatus : Host().Ask(peer.uid, packages, shown, client);
  ALOGI("uid %u: %s", peer.uid,
        answer == kGrantedStatus ? "granted" : answer == kNoBridge ? "refused (no elevation bridge)" : answer == kNoHelloStatus ? "refused (no Windows Hello)" : "denied");
  if (answer != kGrantedStatus) {
    SendReply(client, answer == kNoBridge ? kUnavailable : answer == kNoHelloStatus ? kNoHello : answer == kBusyStatus ? kBusy : kDenied);
    close(pidfd);
    return;
  }

  // The command line of the launcher: <pidfd> <fd0> <fd1> <fd2> <terminal> <cwd> <program> args...
  std::vector<std::string> program = request->argv;
  if (program.empty()) {
    const std::string shell = EnvValue(request->env, "SHELL");
    program.push_back(!shell.empty() && shell[0] == '/' && access(shell.c_str(), X_OK) == 0 ? shell : "/system/bin/sh");
  }
  program[0] = Resolve(program[0], request->env, request->cwd);
  std::vector<std::string> args = {"wsa-elevate-exec", "3", std::to_string(request->header.fds[0]), std::to_string(request->header.fds[1]),
                                   std::to_string(request->header.fds[2]), request->header.terminal ? "1" : "0", request->cwd};
  args.insert(args.end(), program.begin(), program.end());
  std::vector<char*> argv, envp;
  for (std::string& a : args) argv.push_back(a.data());
  argv.push_back(nullptr);
  std::vector<std::string> env = request->env;
  for (std::string& e : env) envp.push_back(e.data());
  envp.push_back(nullptr);

  const pid_t child = fork();
  if (child < 0) {
    SendReply(client, kFailed);
    close(pidfd);
    return;
  }
  if (child == 0) {
    // The launcher keeps the client's pidfd as descriptor 3 and nothing else of the daemon.
    if (dup2(pidfd, 3) < 0) _exit(126);
    syscall(__NR_close_range, 4, ~0U, 0);
    execve(kLauncher, argv.data(), envp.data());
    _exit(127);
  }
  close(pidfd);
  SendReply(client, kGranted);

  // Until the command ends: the client's signals go to its process group; a client that goes
  // away hangs it up, as a closed terminal would.
  const int childfd = static_cast<int>(syscall(__NR_pidfd_open, child, 0));
  bool clientGone = false;
  for (;;) {
    pollfd fds[2] = {{childfd, POLLIN, 0}, {clientGone ? -1 : client, POLLIN | POLLRDHUP, 0}};
    if (childfd < 0) break;  // cannot watch: wait for it below
    if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(fds, 2, -1)) < 0) break;
    if (fds[0].revents) break;
    if (!fds[1].revents) continue;
    uint8_t type = 0;
    int32_t number = 0;
    if ((fds[1].revents & POLLIN) && RecvAll(client, &type, 1) && type == kSignal && RecvAll(client, &number, sizeof number)) {
      static constexpr int kAllowed[] = {SIGHUP, SIGINT, SIGQUIT, SIGTERM, SIGKILL, SIGCONT, SIGTSTP, SIGWINCH, SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2};
      if (std::find(std::begin(kAllowed), std::end(kAllowed), number) != std::end(kAllowed) && kill(-child, number) != 0) kill(child, number);
      continue;
    }
    clientGone = true;
    if (kill(-child, SIGHUP) != 0) kill(child, SIGHUP);
  }
  int status = 0;
  (void)TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(waitpid(child, &status, 0));
  if (childfd >= 0) close(childfd);
  if (!clientGone) {
    const uint8_t exited = kExited;
    const int32_t code = status;
    (void)(SendAll(client, &exited, 1) && SendAll(client, &code, sizeof code));
  }
  ALOGI("uid %u: the elevated command ended (status 0x%x)", peer.uid, status);
}

}  // namespace
}  // namespace wsa::elevate

int main() {
  using namespace wsa::elevate;
  signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);
  const int listener = android_get_control_socket(kSocketName);
  if (listener < 0 || listen(listener, 8) != 0) {
    ALOGE("No control socket %s: %s", kSocketName, strerror(errno));
    return 1;
  }
  SetSuLink(false);  // until a bridge says otherwise
  Host().Start();
  RegistrationHost().Start();
  ALOGI("ready");
  for (;;) {
    const int client = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(accept4(listener, nullptr, nullptr, SOCK_CLOEXEC));
    if (client < 0) continue;
    std::thread([client] {
      Serve(client);
      close(client);
    }).detach();
  }
}
```

```cpp
// wsa-elevate-exec: started by wsa-elevated only, after Windows Hello said yes. Its executable's
// label makes the exec enter the elevated domain (sepolicy wsa_elevate.te).
//
//   wsa-elevate-exec <pidfd> <fd0> <fd1> <fd2> <terminal 0|1> <cwd> <program> [arguments...]
//
// <pidfd> (inherited) refers to the client process; its descriptors <fd0..2> become 0, 1 and 2.
//
//   wsa-elevate-exec --gsf-id
//
// prints the Google Services Framework ID from Play services' Checkin.xml and nothing else
// (for WSA-Next's registration app, protocol.h); exits 1 while there is none.

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <grp.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/inotify.h>
#include <sys/ioctl.h>
#include <sys/syscall.h>
#include <termios.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <string>
#include <string_view>

namespace {

int ParseInt(const char* text) {
  char* end = nullptr;
  errno = 0;
  const long value = strtol(text, &end, 10);
  if (errno != 0 || end == text || *end != '\0' || value < -1 || value > 1 << 20) return -2;
  return static_cast<int>(value);
}

constexpr char kGmsPrefs[] = "/data/data/com.google.android.gms/shared_prefs";
constexpr char kCheckin[] = "/data/data/com.google.android.gms/shared_prefs/Checkin.xml";

// <string name="android_id">1234567890123456789</string> in Play services' check-in preferences;
// empty while they have not checked in (no file, no entry, or 0).
std::string ReadGsfId() {
  const int fd = open(kCheckin, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC);
  if (fd < 0) return {};
  std::string text;
  char buffer[4096];
  ssize_t n = 0;
  while (text.size() < 256 * 1024 && (n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(read(fd, buffer, sizeof buffer))) > 0) text.append(buffer, static_cast<size_t>(n));
  close(fd);
  constexpr std::string_view kKey = "name=\"android_id\"";
  size_t p = text.find(kKey);
  if (p == std::string::npos) return {};
  p = text.find_first_of("0123456789<", p + kKey.size());  // past '>' or value="
  if (p == std::string::npos || text[p] == '<') return {};
  const size_t end = text.find_first_not_of("0123456789", p);
  std::string id = text.substr(p, end == std::string::npos ? std::string::npos : end - p);
  if (id.empty() || id.size() > 20 || id == "0") return {};
  return id;
}

// Play services announce CHECKIN_COMPLETE before their preferences reach the disk
// (SharedPreferences.apply), so the registration app may ask first: then this waits for
// Checkin.xml to be written (inotify), at most kWaitMs - the time a broadcast receiver has.
int PrintGsfId() {
  constexpr int kWaitMs = 20000;
  const int watch = inotify_init1(IN_CLOEXEC | IN_NONBLOCK);
  if (watch >= 0) inotify_add_watch(watch, kGmsPrefs, IN_CLOSE_WRITE | IN_MOVED_TO);  // before the first read
  timespec start{};
  clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &start);
  for (;;) {
    const std::string id = ReadGsfId();
    if (!id.empty()) {
      if (watch >= 0) close(watch);
      return fwrite(id.data(), 1, id.size(), stdout) == id.size() && fflush(stdout) == 0 ? 0 : 1;
    }
    timespec now{};
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &now);
    const long elapsed = (now.tv_sec - start.tv_sec) * 1000 + (now.tv_nsec - start.tv_nsec) / 1000000;
    pollfd changed{watch, POLLIN, 0};
    if (watch < 0 || elapsed >= kWaitMs || TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(&changed, 1, static_cast<int>(kWaitMs - elapsed))) <= 0) {
      if (watch >= 0) close(watch);
      return 1;
    }
    char events[4096];
    while (read(watch, events, sizeof events) > 0) {
    }  // any change in the folder: read the file again
  }
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  if (getuid() != 0) return 126;
  if (argc == 2 && strcmp(argv[1], "--gsf-id") == 0) return PrintGsfId();
  if (argc < 8) return 126;
  const int pidfd = ParseInt(argv[1]);
  const int fds[3] = {ParseInt(argv[2]), ParseInt(argv[3]), ParseInt(argv[4])};
  const bool terminal = strcmp(argv[5], "1") == 0;
  if (pidfd < 0 || fds[0] < 0 || fds[1] < 0 || fds[2] < 0) return 126;

  int taken[3];
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
    taken[i] = static_cast<int>(syscall(__NR_pidfd_getfd, pidfd, fds[i], 0));
    if (taken[i] < 0) return 125;  // the client went away
  }
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
    if (dup2(taken[i], i) < 0) return 125;
  }
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
    if (taken[i] > 2) close(taken[i]);
  }
  close(pidfd);

  // Root as root logs in: none of the daemon's supplementary groups.
  const gid_t rootGroup = 0;
  setgroups(1, &rootGroup);
  setsid();
  if (terminal) ioctl(0, TIOCSCTTY, 0);
  if (chdir(argv[6]) != 0 && chdir("/") != 0) return 126;
  execv(argv[7], argv + 7);
  fprintf(stderr, "0: %s: %s\n", argv[7], strerror(errno));
  return 127;
}
```

```h
// Root for apps, confirmed on Windows with Windows Hello.
//
//   0 (in the app's process)  --unix socket /dev/socket/wsa_elevate-->  wsa-elevated (daemon)
//   wsa-elevated  --vsock "WSEV"-->  WSA-Next.exe host (Windows Hello with the app and the command)
//   granted: wsa-elevated starts wsa-elevate-exec, whose executable enters the elevated domain;
//   it takes the client's terminal or stdio from the client process itself (pidfd_getfd) and
//   runs the command. The client relays the terminal, the exit status and, without a terminal,
//   signals - no descriptor of the app ever passes through the daemon.
//
// The daemon learns who asks from the kernel (SO_PEERCRED), never from the request.
#pragma once

#include <stdint.h>

namespace wsa::elevate {

constexpr char kSocketName[] = "wsa_elevate";  // /dev/socket/wsa_elevate, created by init
constexpr char kSocketPath[] = "/dev/socket/wsa_elevate";
constexpr char kLauncher[] = "/system_ext/bin/wsa-elevate-exec";

constexpr uint32_t kRequestMagic = 0x4c455357;  // 'W','S','E','L'
constexpr uint32_t kVersion = 1;
constexpr uint32_t kMaxStrings = 256 * 1024;
constexpr uint32_t kMaxCount = 4096;

// client -> daemon, followed by `length` bytes: cwd\0, argc arguments\0, envc variables\0.
struct Request {
  uint32_t magic = kRequestMagic;
  uint32_t version = kVersion;
  int32_t fds[3] = {0, 1, 2};  // the client's descriptors that become 0, 1 and 2 of the command
  int32_t terminal = 0;        // 1: fds[0] is a terminal of its own (a pty) to make controlling
  uint32_t argc = 0;           // 0: an interactive shell
  uint32_t envc = 0;
  uint32_t length = 0;
};

// daemon -> client: one byte; kExited is followed by the int32 wait status.
enum Reply : uint8_t {
  kGranted = 'G',
  kDenied = 'D',
  kUnavailable = 'U',  // root for Android apps is off in WSA-Next, or its host is not running
  kBusy = 'B',
  kNoHello = 'H',      // Windows Hello is not set up on Windows
  kInvalid = 'I',
  kFailed = 'F',
  kExited = 'X',
};

// client -> daemon after kGranted (no terminal of its own): kSignal, then the int32 signal.
constexpr uint8_t kSignal = 'S';

// The Google Services Framework ID for WSA-Next's "Register this PC with Google Play"
// notification (device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/registration). Current Play services give it only to
// Google-signed apps, so that app asks here: client -> daemon the four bytes "GFID"; daemon ->
// client kGranted, one length byte and the decimal ID, or kDenied / kFailed. No Windows Hello:
// it is the ID the user copies to Google's registration page, given to that one app only.
constexpr uint32_t kGsfIdMagic = 0x44494647;  // 'G','F','I','D'
constexpr char kRegistrationPackage[] = "org.wsanext.registration";

// The same app asks for the notice on Windows: a click on Android's own notification does not
// come back to Android there. Client -> daemon "RGWN"; the daemon reads the ID itself and hands it
// to WSA-Next on Windows over vsock port "WSRG" (daemon -> host "RGID", one length byte, the
// decimal ID; host -> daemon one byte), whose notification copies the ID and opens Google's page
// in the Windows browser. Daemon -> client: that byte - kRegistrationShown, kRegistrationDone
// (registered from Windows before), kRegistrationNotShown (no icon to show it) - or kUnavailable
// (no WSA-Next host), kDenied, kFailed (no ID yet).
constexpr uint32_t kRegisterOnWindowsMagic = 0x4E574752;  // 'R','G','W','N'
constexpr uint32_t kRegistrationPort = 0x57535247;        // "WSRG"
constexpr uint8_t kRegistrationShown = 'S';
constexpr uint8_t kRegistrationDone = 'O';  // not 'D': kDenied
constexpr uint8_t kRegistrationNotShown = 'N';
constexpr char kGsfIdOption[] = "--gsf-id";  // wsa-elevate-exec --gsf-id prints it

}  // namespace wsa::elevate
```

```rc
# WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
# Root for apps, confirmed on Windows with Windows Hello (device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/elevate).

# /dev/wsa/bin: last on everyone's PATH and empty. While "su for root apps" is on in WSA-Next on
# Windows, the daemon puts the link su -> /system_ext/bin/0 there; /dev is one tmpfs for every
# process, so apps see it at once and nothing else of the system changes. The PATH is the
# default one plus that folder (set before zygote and adbd start, which pass it on).
on init
    mkdir /dev/wsa 0755 root root
    mkdir /dev/wsa/bin 0755 root root
    export PATH /product/bin:/apex/com.android.runtime/bin:/apex/com.android.art/bin:/system_ext/bin:/system/bin:/system/xbin:/odm/bin:/vendor/bin:/vendor/xbin:/dev/wsa/bin

# Root with the daemon's narrow SELinux domain; group package_info reads packages.list.
service wsa-elevated /system_ext/bin/wsa-elevated
    class main
    user root
    group root package_info
    socket wsa_elevate stream 0666 root root
```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/elevate/zero.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * Copyright 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
 *
 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
 * You may obtain a copy of the License at
 *
 *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.
 */

// 0: runs a command (or a shell) as root - uid 0 - once Windows Hello on the PC says yes.
//
//   0                  an interactive root shell
//   0 -c "command"     the command through sh
//   0 program [args]   the program
//
// Called as "su" (/dev/wsa/bin/su, present only while "su for root apps" is on in WSA-Next) it
// speaks su's syntax, so root apps and libsu work unchanged.
//
// On a terminal the root command gets a terminal of its own (a pty this process relays), so
// line editing, job control and Ctrl+C behave as usual. Exits with the command's status.

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/ioctl.h>
#include <sys/signalfd.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <sys/un.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <termios.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "protocol.h"

extern char** environ;

namespace {

using namespace wsa::elevate;

termios gSaved;
bool gRaw = false;

void Restore() {
  if (gRaw) tcsetattr(STDIN_FILENO, TCSAFLUSH, &gSaved);
  gRaw = false;
}

bool WriteAll(int fd, const void* data, size_t size) {
  const auto* p = static_cast<const char*>(data);
  while (size) {
    const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(write(fd, p, size));
    if (n <= 0) return false;
    p += n;
    size -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
  }
  return true;
}

bool ReadAll(int fd, void* data, size_t size) {
  auto* p = static_cast<char*>(data);
  while (size) {
    const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(read(fd, p, size));
    if (n <= 0) return false;
    p += n;
    size -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
  }
  return true;
}

int Usage() {
  fprintf(stderr,
          "usage: 0                  interactive root shell\n"
          "       0 -c \"command\"     run the command through sh\n"
          "       0 program [args]   run the program\n"
          "Each request is confirmed on Windows with Windows Hello (WSA-Next: Android > Root for apps).\n");
  return 2;
}

int Refused(uint8_t reply) {
  const char* why = reply == kDenied        ? "denied on Windows"
                    : reply == kUnavailable ? "root for Android apps is off (WSA-Next on Windows: Android > Root for apps)"
                    : reply == kBusy        ? "another request is waiting for Windows Hello"
                    : reply == kNoHello     ? "Windows Hello is not set up on Windows"
                    : reply == kInvalid     ? "invalid request"
                                            : "failed";
  fprintf(stderr, "0: %s\n", why);
  return 1;
}

int ExitCode(int32_t status) {
  if (WIFEXITED(status)) return WEXITSTATUS(status);
  if (WIFSIGNALED(status)) return 128 + WTERMSIG(status);
  return 1;
}

// Called as "su" (the link WSA-Next makes for root apps while "su for root apps" is on): the
// syntax root apps and libraries such as libsu use. Returns an exit code, or -1 to go on.
//   su [options] [-] [0|root] [command [args...]]
//   -c|--command cmd, -s|--shell sh, -v|--version, -V; accepted and needless here: -, -l,
//   --login, -p, -m, --preserve-environment, --mount-master, -mm, -M, -Z|--context ctx
int ParseSu(int argc, char** argv, std::vector<std::string>& command) {
  std::string shell, run;
  bool hasRun = false;
  int i = 1;
  for (; i < argc; ++i) {
    const std::string a = argv[i];
    if (a == "-c" || a == "--command" || a == "-s" || a == "--shell" || a == "-Z" || a == "--context") {
      if (++i >= argc) return Usage();
      if (a == "-c" || a == "--command") run = argv[i], hasRun = true;
      else if (a == "-s" || a == "--shell") shell = argv[i];
    } else if (a.rfind("--command=", 0) == 0) {
      run = a.substr(10), hasRun = true;
    } else if (a == "-" || a == "-l" || a == "--login" || a == "-p" || a == "-m" || a == "--preserve-environment" ||
               a == "--mount-master" || a == "-mm" || a == "-M") {
      // The environment is passed anyway; there is one mount namespace view to give.
    } else if (a == "-v" || a == "--version") {
      printf("0:WSA-Next\n");
      return 0;
    } else if (a == "-V") {
      printf("1\n");
      return 0;
    } else if (a == "-h" || a == "--help") {
      return Usage();
    } else if (a == "--") {
      ++i;
      break;
    } else if (!a.empty() && a[0] == '-') {
      fprintf(stderr, "su: unknown option %s\n", a.c_str());
      return 2;
    } else {
      break;
    }
  }
  if (i < argc) {  // the user: there is one, root
    if (strcmp(argv[i], "0") != 0 && strcmp(argv[i], "root") != 0) {
      fprintf(stderr, "su: only root (0)\n");
      return 1;
    }
    ++i;
  }
  if (hasRun) command = {shell.empty() ? "sh" : shell, "-c", run};
  else if (i < argc) command.assign(argv + i, argv + argc);  // "su 0 command args", as AOSP's su
  else if (!shell.empty()) command = {shell};
  return -1;
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  std::vector<std::string> command;
  const char* name = strrchr(argv[0], '/');
  name = name ? name + 1 : argv[0];
  if (!strcmp(name, "su")) {
    if (const int code = ParseSu(argc, argv, command); code >= 0) return code;
  } else if (argc >= 2 && (!strcmp(argv[1], "-h") || !strcmp(argv[1], "--help"))) {
    return Usage();
  } else if (argc >= 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "-c")) {
    if (argc != 3) return Usage();
    command = {"sh", "-c", argv[2]};
  } else {
    for (int i = (argc >= 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "--")) ? 2 : 1; i < argc; ++i) command.emplace_back(argv[i]);
  }

  const int sock = socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
  sockaddr_un addr{};
  addr.sun_family = AF_UNIX;
  strncpy(addr.sun_path, kSocketPath, sizeof addr.sun_path - 1);
  if (sock < 0 || connect(sock, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&addr), sizeof addr) != 0) {
    fprintf(stderr, "0: the elevation service is not available (%s)\n", strerror(errno));
    return 1;
  }

  // A terminal of its own for the root command when this one runs on a terminal.
  const bool onTerminal = isatty(STDIN_FILENO) && isatty(STDOUT_FILENO);
  int master = -1, slave = -1;
  if (onTerminal) {
    char name[64] = {};
    master = posix_openpt(O_RDWR | O_NOCTTY | O_CLOEXEC);
    if (master < 0 || grantpt(master) != 0 || unlockpt(master) != 0 || ptsname_r(master, name, sizeof name) != 0 ||
        (slave = open(name, O_RDWR | O_NOCTTY | O_CLOEXEC)) < 0) {
      fprintf(stderr, "0: no pseudo-terminal: %s\n", strerror(errno));
      return 1;
    }
    termios mode;
    if (tcgetattr(STDIN_FILENO, &mode) == 0) tcsetattr(slave, TCSANOW, &mode);
    winsize size;
    if (ioctl(STDIN_FILENO, TIOCGWINSZ, &size) == 0) ioctl(master, TIOCSWINSZ, &size);
  }

  Request request;
  if (onTerminal) {
    request.fds[0] = request.fds[1] = slave;
    request.fds[2] = isatty(STDERR_FILENO) ? slave : STDERR_FILENO;
    request.terminal = 1;
  }
  char cwd[4096] = "/";
  if (!getcwd(cwd, sizeof cwd)) strcpy(cwd, "/");
  std::string strings(cwd);
  strings += '\0';
  for (const std::string& arg : command) strings += arg + '\0';
  uint32_t envc = 0;
  for (char** e = environ; e && *e; ++e, ++envc) strings += std::string(*e) + '\0';
  request.argc = static_cast<uint32_t>(command.size());
  request.envc = envc;
  request.length = static_cast<uint32_t>(strings.size());
  if (strings.size() > kMaxStrings || !WriteAll(sock, &request, sizeof request) || !WriteAll(sock, strings.data(), strings.size())) {
    fprintf(stderr, "0: the request is too large or the service went away\n");
    return 1;
  }

  // Waits for Windows Hello. Signals stay deliverable meanwhile: Ctrl+C here cancels the request.
  uint8_t reply = 0;
  if (!ReadAll(sock, &reply, 1)) return Refused(kFailed);
  if (reply != kGranted) return Refused(reply);

  sigset_t watched;
  sigemptyset(&watched);
  for (const int s : {SIGWINCH, SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGQUIT, SIGTSTP, SIGCONT, SIGUSR1, SIGUSR2}) sigaddset(&watched, s);
  sigprocmask(SIG_BLOCK, &watched, nullptr);
  const int signals = signalfd(-1, &watched, SFD_CLOEXEC);

  if (onTerminal) {
    // The root command has taken the pty's other end: this one only relays, in raw mode.
    if (tcgetattr(STDIN_FILENO, &gSaved) == 0) {
      termios raw = gSaved;
      cfmakeraw(&raw);
      gRaw = tcsetattr(STDIN_FILENO, TCSAFLUSH, &raw) == 0;
      atexit(Restore);
    }
  }

  bool inputOpen = onTerminal, outputOpen = onTerminal;
  int32_t status = 0;
  bool exited = false;
  char buffer[16384];
  while (!exited) {
    pollfd fds[4] = {{sock, POLLIN, 0}, {signals, POLLIN, 0}, {inputOpen ? STDIN_FILENO : -1, POLLIN, 0}, {outputOpen ? master : -1, POLLIN, 0}};
    if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(fds, 4, -1)) < 0) break;
    if (fds[3].revents) {
      const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(read(master, buffer, sizeof buffer));
      if (n > 0) WriteAll(STDOUT_FILENO, buffer, static_cast<size_t>(n));
      else outputOpen = false;  // EIO: nothing holds the terminal any more
    }
    if (fds[2].revents) {
      const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(read(STDIN_FILENO, buffer, sizeof buffer));
      if (n > 0) WriteAll(master, buffer, static_cast<size_t>(n));
      else inputOpen = false;
    }
    if (fds[1].revents) {
      signalfd_siginfo info;
      if (ReadAll(signals, &info, sizeof info)) {
        const int number = static_cast<int>(info.ssi_signo);
        if (number == SIGWINCH && onTerminal) {
          winsize size;
          if (ioctl(STDIN_FILENO, TIOCGWINSZ, &size) == 0) ioctl(master, TIOCSWINSZ, &size);
        } else if (!onTerminal || number == SIGTERM || number == SIGHUP) {
          // On a terminal, Ctrl+C and friends are bytes for the pty; these come from outside.
          const uint8_t type = kSignal;
          const int32_t value = number;
          WriteAll(sock, &type, 1);
          WriteAll(sock, &value, sizeof value);
        }
      }
    }
    if (fds[0].revents) {
      uint8_t type = 0;
      if (ReadAll(sock, &type, 1) && type == kExited && ReadAll(sock, &status, sizeof status)) exited = true;
      else break;  // the service went away
    }
  }
  if (onTerminal && outputOpen) {
    // What the command wrote last is still in the pty.
    fcntl(master, F_SETFL, fcntl(master, F_GETFL) | O_NONBLOCK);
    for (ssize_t n; (n = read(master, buffer, sizeof buffer)) > 0;) WriteAll(STDOUT_FILENO, buffer, static_cast<size_t>(n));
  }
  Restore();
  return exited ? ExitCode(status) : 1;
}
```
