`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/fingerprint/WsaFingerprint.cpp`:

```cpp
/*
 * Copyright 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
 *
 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
 * You may obtain a copy of the License at
 *
 *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.
 */
#define LOG_TAG "android.hardware.biometrics.fingerprint.wsa"

#include "WsaFingerprint.h"

#include <android-base/parseint.h>
#include <android-base/properties.h>
#include <android-base/strings.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>  // before linux/vm_sockets.h, which needs struct sockaddr
#include <unistd.h>

#include <linux/vm_sockets.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <random>

#include "log/log.h"

namespace aidl::android::hardware::biometrics::fingerprint::wsa {
namespace {

// Wire protocol of src/biometrics/Protocol.h on the Windows host: an 8-byte header, then an
// optional UTF-8 payload (the prompt of a request).
constexpr uint32_t kBridgePort = 0x57534650;  // "WSFP"
constexpr uint32_t kMagic = 0x50465357;       // 'W','S','F','P' little-endian
constexpr uint8_t kOpAuthenticate = 3;        // HAL -> bridge request, bridge -> HAL answer
constexpr uint8_t kOpAvailability = 4;        // bridge -> HAL, whenever it changes
constexpr uint8_t kOpCancel = 5;              // HAL -> bridge: close the Windows Hello dialog
constexpr uint8_t kStatusOk = 0;
constexpr uint8_t kStatusVerified = 1;
constexpr uint8_t kStatusCanceled = 2;
constexpr uint8_t kStatusNotAvailable = 3;
constexpr uint8_t kStatusBusy = 4;
constexpr uint8_t kNoBridge = 0xFF;  // local: no bridge connected, or it went away

struct FrameHeader {
  uint32_t magic = kMagic;
  uint8_t op = 0;
  uint8_t status = 0;
  uint16_t payloadLen = 0;
};
static_assert(sizeof(FrameHeader) == 8);

constexpr char kAvailableProperty[] = "sys.wsa.fingerprint.hello";
constexpr char kStatePrefix[] = "persist.wsa.fingerprint.u";
constexpr int32_t kTemplateId = 1;  // the one template: "Windows Hello"

int64_t RandomId() {
  std::random_device rd;
  const uint64_t v = (static_cast<uint64_t>(rd()) << 32) | static_cast<uint64_t>(rd());
  return static_cast<int64_t>(v == 0 ? 1 : v);
}

bool SendAll(int fd, const void* data, size_t size) {
  const auto* p = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(data);
  size_t done = 0;
  while (done < size) {
    const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(send(fd, p + done, size - done, MSG_NOSIGNAL));
    if (n <= 0) return false;
    done += static_cast<size_t>(n);
  }
  return true;
}

bool RecvAll(int fd, void* data, size_t size) {
  auto* p = static_cast<uint8_t*>(data);
  size_t done = 0;
  while (done < size) {
    const ssize_t n = TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(recv(fd, p + done, size - done, 0));
    if (n <= 0) return false;
    done += static_cast<size_t>(n);
  }
  return true;
}

// The connection from the Windows Hello bridge. One thread accepts it and reads what the bridge
// sends (availability pushes, verification answers); requests are written from the session
// threads. All waits are on file descriptors or a condition variable, without timeouts.
class HelloLink {
 public:
  static HelloLink& Get() {
    static HelloLink* link = new HelloLink();  // lives as long as the service
    return *link;
  }

  bool Available() {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    return mAvailable;
  }

  // Asks Windows Hello. Returns its answer, kStatusCanceled when `canceled` was set (the dialog is
  // closed), or kNoBridge when the bridge is not there or goes away meanwhile.
  uint8_t Authenticate(const std::string& prompt, const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>& canceled) {
    std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mLock);
    if (mConnection < 0) return kNoBridge;
    const uint16_t length = static_cast<uint16_t>(std::min<size_t>(prompt.size(), 512));
    const FrameHeader request{kMagic, kOpAuthenticate, 0, length};
    if (!SendAll(mConnection, &request, sizeof request) || !SendAll(mConnection, prompt.data(), length)) return kNoBridge;
    const uint64_t generation = mGeneration;
    mAnswer.reset();
    mWaiting = true;
    bool cancelSent = false;
    for (;;) {
      mChanged.wait(lock, [&] { return mAnswer.has_value() || mGeneration != generation || (canceled->load() && !cancelSent); });
      if (mAnswer.has_value()) break;
      if (mGeneration != generation) {
        mWaiting = false;
        return kNoBridge;
      }
      // Canceled: ask Windows to close the dialog; its answer ("canceled") ends the wait.
      const FrameHeader cancel{kMagic, kOpCancel, 0, 0};
      cancelSent = true;
      if (!SendAll(mConnection, &cancel, sizeof cancel)) {
        mWaiting = false;
        return kStatusCanceled;
      }
    }
    mWaiting = false;
    return canceled->load() ? kStatusCanceled : *mAnswer;
  }

  // Waits while `waiting` holds, without asking Windows. True when it stopped holding (ask now),
  // false when the operation was canceled meanwhile.
  bool WaitWhile(const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>& canceled, const std::atomic<bool>& waiting) {
    std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mLock);
    mChanged.wait(lock, [&] { return canceled->load() || !waiting.load(); });
    return !canceled->load();
  }

  // Wakes a waiting Authenticate or WaitWhile (the cancellation signal was set, or the context
  // changed). Taking the lock first orders this after the waiter's predicate check: either it sees
  // the change or it is already waiting.
  void Notify() {
    { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock); }
    mChanged.notify_all();
  }

 private:
  HelloLink() {
    ::android::base::SetProperty(kAvailableProperty, "0");
    std::thread(&HelloLink::Serve, this).detach();
  }

  void SetAvailableLocked(bool available) {
    if (available == mAvailable) return;
    mAvailable = available;
    ::android::base::SetProperty(kAvailableProperty, available ? "1" : "0");
    ALOGI("Windows Hello %s", available ? "available" : "not available");
  }

  void DropLocked() {
    if (mConnection >= 0) ::close(mConnection);
    mConnection = -1;
    ++mGeneration;  // fails a waiting request
    SetAvailableLocked(false);
    mChanged.notify_all();
  }

  void Serve() {
    const int listener = socket(AF_VSOCK, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
    sockaddr_vm addr{};
    addr.svm_family = AF_VSOCK;
    addr.svm_cid = VMADDR_CID_ANY;
    addr.svm_port = kBridgePort;
    if (listener < 0 || bind(listener, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&addr), sizeof addr) != 0 || listen(listener, 1) != 0) {
      ALOGE("Cannot listen on vsock port 0x%08x: %s", kBridgePort, strerror(errno));
      return;
    }
    for (;;) {
      int connection = -1;
      {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
        connection = mConnection;
      }
      pollfd fds[2] = {};
      fds[0].fd = listener;
      fds[0].events = POLLIN;
      fds[1].fd = connection;  // -1: ignored by poll
      fds[1].events = POLLIN | POLLRDHUP;
      if (TEMP_FAILURE_RETRY(poll(fds, 2, -1)) < 0) continue;

      if (fds[0].revents & POLLIN) {
        const int fd = accept4(listener, nullptr, nullptr, SOCK_CLOEXEC);
        if (fd >= 0) {
          std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
          DropLocked();  // a new bridge replaces the previous connection
          mConnection = fd;
          ALOGI("The Windows Hello bridge connected");
        }
        continue;
      }
      if (connection < 0 || fds[1].revents == 0) continue;
      FrameHeader frame{};
      // Data first: a last frame may come with the hangup (read until recv says the end).
      bool ok = (fds[1].revents & POLLIN) && RecvAll(connection, &frame, sizeof frame) && frame.magic == kMagic;
      for (uint16_t left = ok ? frame.payloadLen : 0; ok && left > 0;) {  // no payload is expected: skip it
        uint8_t skip[64];
        const size_t n = std::min<size_t>(left, sizeof skip);
        ok = RecvAll(connection, skip, n);
        left = static_cast<uint16_t>(left - n);
      }
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
      if (connection != mConnection) continue;
      if (!ok) {
        ALOGI("The Windows Hello bridge disconnected");
        DropLocked();
      } else if (frame.op == kOpAvailability) {
        SetAvailableLocked(frame.status == kStatusOk);
      } else if (frame.op == kOpAuthenticate && mWaiting) {
        mAnswer = frame.status;
        mChanged.notify_all();
      }
    }
  }

  std::mutex mLock;
  std::condition_variable mChanged;
  int mConnection = -1;
  uint64_t mGeneration = 0;  // advanced whenever the connection ends
  bool mAvailable = false;
  bool mWaiting = false;
  std::optional<uint8_t> mAnswer;
};

class WsaCancelSignal : public common::BnCancellationSignal {
 public:
  explicit WsaCancelSignal(std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>> flag) : mFlag(std::move(flag)) {}
  ndk::ScopedAStatus cancel() override {
    mFlag->store(true);
    HelloLink::Get().Notify();
    return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
  }

 private:
  std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>> mFlag;
};

// The lock screen listens for a finger also while it is not shown: the screen is off or dozing
// (display state NO_UI, AOD, SCREENSAVER) or it is not known yet, so that a touch of the sensor
// wakes and unlocks a phone. A phone's sensor then waits silently for a finger; opening Windows
// Hello for it asked the person every time Android went to sleep (each 15 seconds without input,
// and whenever the last Android window closed). So the HAL waits too, and asks Windows only once
// the lock screen is shown. Apps (BiometricPrompt) are asked at once, as before.
bool WaitsForLockScreen(const common::OperationContext& context) {
  return context.reason == common::OperationReason::KEYGUARD && context.displayState != common::DisplayState::LOCKSCREEN;
}

std::string StateProperty(int32_t userId) { return kStatePrefix + std::to_string(userId); }

// "<authenticator id>:<template>,<template>..."
UserState LoadState(int32_t userId) {
  UserState state;
  const std::string value = ::android::base::GetProperty(StateProperty(userId), "");
  const std::vector<std::string> parts = ::android::base::Split(value, ":");
  if (parts.size() == 2) {
    ::android::base::ParseInt(parts[0], &state.authenticatorId);
    for (const std::string& id : ::android::base::Split(parts[1], ",")) {
      int32_t template_id = 0;
      if (::android::base::ParseInt(id, &template_id) && template_id > 0) state.enrollments.push_back(template_id);
    }
  }
  if (state.authenticatorId == 0) state.authenticatorId = RandomId();
  return state;
}

}  // namespace

WsaSession::WsaSession(int32_t /*sensorId: there is only one*/, int32_t userId, std::shared_ptr<ISessionCallback> cb)
    : mUserId(userId), mCb(std::move(cb)), mState(LoadState(userId)) {}

WsaSession::~WsaSession() { JoinWorker(); }

void WsaSession::JoinWorker() {
  if (!mWorker.joinable()) return;
  // Harmless when the operation has ended already; ends the wait for Windows when it has not.
  if (mWorkerCanceled && !mWorkerCanceled->exchange(true)) HelloLink::Get().Notify();
  mWorker.join();
  mWorkerCanceled.reset();
}

void WsaSession::StartWorker(std::function<void(const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>&)> work,
                             std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  JoinWorker();
  auto canceled = std::make_shared<std::atomic<bool>>(false);
  *out = ndk::SharedRefBase::make<WsaCancelSignal>(canceled);
  mWorkerCanceled = canceled;
  mWorker = std::thread([work = std::move(work), canceled] { work(canceled); });
}

void WsaSession::Save() {
  std::string ids;
  for (const int32_t id : mState.enrollments) ids += (ids.empty() ? "" : ",") + std::to_string(id);
  if (!::android::base::SetProperty(StateProperty(mUserId), std::to_string(mState.authenticatorId) + ":" + ids)) {
    ALOGE("Could not save the fingerprint state of user %d", mUserId);
  }
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::generateChallenge() {
  mCb->onChallengeGenerated(RandomId());
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::revokeChallenge(int64_t challenge) {
  mCb->onChallengeRevoked(challenge);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

// Linking needs Windows Hello to be there, not a verification (every use is verified).
void WsaSession::Enroll() {
  if (!HelloLink::Get().Available()) {
    ALOGW("enroll: Windows Hello is not available");
    mCb->onError(Error::HW_UNAVAILABLE, 0);
    return;
  }
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    if (std::find(mState.enrollments.begin(), mState.enrollments.end(), kTemplateId) == mState.enrollments.end()) {
      mState.enrollments.push_back(kTemplateId);
    }
    Save();
  }
  ALOGI("enrolled: Windows Hello linked for user %d", mUserId);
  mCb->onEnrollmentProgress(kTemplateId, 0);
}

void WsaSession::Authenticate(int64_t operationId, const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>& canceled) {
  int64_t authenticatorId = 0;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    if (mState.enrollments.empty()) {
      mCb->onError(Error::UNABLE_TO_PROCESS, 0);
      return;
    }
    authenticatorId = mState.authenticatorId;
  }
  if (mWaitForLockScreen.load()) {
    ALOGI("authenticate: the lock screen asks while it is not shown, waiting like a sensor");
    if (!HelloLink::Get().WaitWhile(canceled, mWaitForLockScreen)) {
      mCb->onError(Error::CANCELED, 0);
      return;
    }
    ALOGI("authenticate: the lock screen is shown, asking Windows Hello");
  }
  const uint8_t status = HelloLink::Get().Authenticate("Android in WSA-Next asks you to verify your identity", canceled);
  if (status == kStatusCanceled) {
    mCb->onError(Error::CANCELED, 0);
    return;
  }
  if (status == kNoBridge || status == kStatusNotAvailable || status == kStatusBusy) {
    mCb->onError(Error::HW_UNAVAILABLE, 0);
    return;
  }
  if (status != kStatusVerified) {
    mCb->onAuthenticationFailed();
    return;
  }
  // No TEE can sign this token: the sensor is WEAK, so the framework never hands it to KeyMint.
  keymaster::HardwareAuthToken hat;
  hat.challenge = operationId;
  hat.userId = mUserId;
  hat.authenticatorId = authenticatorId;
  hat.authenticatorType = keymaster::HardwareAuthenticatorType::FINGERPRINT;
  hat.timestamp.milliSeconds =
      std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
  mCb->onAuthenticationSucceeded(kTemplateId, hat);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::enroll(const keymaster::HardwareAuthToken& /*hat*/,
                                      std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  StartWorker([this](const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>&) { Enroll(); }, out);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::authenticate(int64_t operationId,
                                            std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  StartAuthenticate(operationId, false, out);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

void WsaSession::StartAuthenticate(int64_t operationId, bool waitForLockScreen,
                                   std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  JoinWorker();  // the previous operation ends first: the flag below belongs to the new one only
  mWaitForLockScreen = waitForLockScreen;
  StartWorker([this, operationId](const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>& canceled) { Authenticate(operationId, canceled); }, out);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::detectInteraction(std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  *out = ndk::SharedRefBase::make<WsaCancelSignal>(std::make_shared<std::atomic<bool>>(false));
  mCb->onError(Error::UNABLE_TO_PROCESS, 0);  // not supported (supportsDetectInteraction = false)
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::enumerateEnrollments() {
  std::vector<int32_t> ids;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    ids = mState.enrollments;
  }
  mCb->onEnrollmentsEnumerated(ids);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::removeEnrollments(const std::vector<int32_t>& enrollmentIds) {
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    for (const int32_t id : enrollmentIds) {
      mState.enrollments.erase(std::remove(mState.enrollments.begin(), mState.enrollments.end(), id), mState.enrollments.end());
    }
    Save();
  }
  mCb->onEnrollmentsRemoved(enrollmentIds);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::getAuthenticatorId() {
  int64_t id = 0;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    id = mState.authenticatorId;
  }
  mCb->onAuthenticatorIdRetrieved(id);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::invalidateAuthenticatorId() {
  int64_t id = 0;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> guard(mLock);
    mState.authenticatorId = RandomId();
    id = mState.authenticatorId;
    Save();
  }
  mCb->onAuthenticatorIdInvalidated(id);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::resetLockout(const keymaster::HardwareAuthToken& /*hat*/) {
  mCb->onLockoutCleared();  // Windows Hello keeps its own lockout
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::close() {
  JoinWorker();
  mCb->onSessionClosed();
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::onPointerDown(int32_t, int32_t, int32_t, float, float) { return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok(); }
ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::onPointerUp(int32_t) { return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok(); }
ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::onUiReady() { return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok(); }

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::authenticateWithContext(int64_t operationId, const common::OperationContext& context,
                                                       std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  ALOGI("authenticate: reason %d, display state %d", static_cast<int>(context.reason), static_cast<int>(context.displayState));
  StartAuthenticate(operationId, WaitsForLockScreen(context), out);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::enrollWithContext(const keymaster::HardwareAuthToken& hat, const common::OperationContext&,
                                                 std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  return enroll(hat, out);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::detectInteractionWithContext(const common::OperationContext&,
                                                            std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) {
  return detectInteraction(out);
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::onPointerDownWithContext(const PointerContext&) { return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok(); }
ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::onPointerUpWithContext(const PointerContext&) { return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok(); }
// The running operation's context changed, e.g. the lock screen came up after the screen woke.
ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::onContextChanged(const common::OperationContext& context) {
  const bool wait = WaitsForLockScreen(context);
  if (mWaitForLockScreen.exchange(wait) != wait) {
    ALOGI("context changed: reason %d, display state %d", static_cast<int>(context.reason), static_cast<int>(context.displayState));
    HelloLink::Get().Notify();
  }
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}
ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::onPointerCancelWithContext(const PointerContext&) { return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok(); }
ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaSession::setIgnoreDisplayTouches(bool) { return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok(); }

WsaFingerprint::WsaFingerprint() { (void)HelloLink::Get(); }  // starts listening for the bridge

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaFingerprint::getSensorProps(std::vector<SensorProps>* out) {
  const common::ComponentInfo hw{"windowsHello", "WSA-Next", "Windows Hello", "", ""};
  // WEAK: verified by Windows, not by an Android TEE (no KeyMint-bound keys).
  const common::CommonProps commonProps{1 /* sensorId */, common::SensorStrength::WEAK,
                                        1 /* maxEnrollmentsPerUser: "Windows Hello" */, {hw}};
  SensorLocation location;
  *out = {{commonProps,
           FingerprintSensorType::REAR,
           {location},
           false /* supportsNavigationGestures */,
           false /* supportsDetectInteraction */,
           false /* halHandlesDisplayTouches */,
           false /* halControlsIllumination */,
           std::nullopt /* touchDetectionParameters */}};
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}

ndk::ScopedAStatus WsaFingerprint::createSession(int32_t sensorId, int32_t userId,
                                                 const std::shared_ptr<ISessionCallback>& cb,
                                                 std::shared_ptr<ISession>* out) {
  *out = ndk::SharedRefBase::make<WsaSession>(sensorId, userId, cb);
  return ndk::ScopedAStatus::ok();
}
```

```h
// Fingerprint HAL of WSA: Windows Hello is the sensor.
//
// Android sees one fingerprint sensor of WEAK strength (the verification happens in Windows, not
// in a TEE that could mint hardware auth tokens for KeyMint) with at most one template per user,
// "Windows Hello". Enrolling links Android to the Windows Hello of the signed-in Windows user; it
// needs no finger and no prompt, because every authentication is verified by Windows Hello itself
// (fingerprint, face or PIN, in Windows' own dialog). WSA-Next's system_server service enrolls it
// automatically, so no Android screen lock is needed (a lock screen would hide WSA's windows).
//
// The Windows side is the Windows Hello bridge of WSA-Next.exe, which connects to this HAL over a
// Hyper-V socket (vsock port "WSFP") when it starts and keeps the connection. It pushes whether
// Windows Hello is available whenever that changes (published in sys.wsa.fingerprint.hello) and
// answers verification requests; nothing here polls. Enrollments and authenticator IDs are kept
// in persist.wsa.fingerprint.u<user>, so the framework finds them again after a restart.

#pragma once

#include <aidl/android/hardware/biometrics/common/BnCancellationSignal.h>
#include <aidl/android/hardware/biometrics/fingerprint/BnFingerprint.h>
#include <aidl/android/hardware/biometrics/fingerprint/BnSession.h>
#include <aidl/android/hardware/biometrics/fingerprint/ISessionCallback.h>

#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

namespace aidl::android::hardware::biometrics::fingerprint::wsa {

namespace common = ::aidl::android::hardware::biometrics::common;
namespace keymaster = ::aidl::android::hardware::keymaster;

// What the HAL remembers per Android user.
struct UserState {
  int64_t authenticatorId = 0;
  std::vector<int32_t> enrollments;
};

class WsaSession : public BnSession {
 public:
  WsaSession(int32_t sensorId, int32_t userId, std::shared_ptr<ISessionCallback> cb);
  ~WsaSession() override;

  ndk::ScopedAStatus generateChallenge() override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus revokeChallenge(int64_t challenge) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus enroll(const keymaster::HardwareAuthToken& hat,
                            std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus authenticate(int64_t operationId,
                                  std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus detectInteraction(
      std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus enumerateEnrollments() override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus removeEnrollments(const std::vector<int32_t>& enrollmentIds) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus getAuthenticatorId() override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus invalidateAuthenticatorId() override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus resetLockout(const keymaster::HardwareAuthToken& hat) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus close() override;

  ndk::ScopedAStatus onPointerDown(int32_t pointerId, int32_t x, int32_t y, float minor,
                                   float major) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus onPointerUp(int32_t pointerId) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus onUiReady() override;

  ndk::ScopedAStatus authenticateWithContext(
      int64_t operationId, const common::OperationContext& context,
      std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus enrollWithContext(
      const keymaster::HardwareAuthToken& hat, const common::OperationContext& context,
      std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus detectInteractionWithContext(
      const common::OperationContext& context,
      std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus onPointerDownWithContext(const PointerContext& context) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus onPointerUpWithContext(const PointerContext& context) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus onContextChanged(const common::OperationContext& context) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus onPointerCancelWithContext(const PointerContext& context) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus setIgnoreDisplayTouches(bool shouldIgnore) override;

 private:
  // One operation at a time. A new operation, close() and the destructor first cancel one that is
  // still running (the Windows Hello dialog closes) and then wait for it: the binder thread, the
  // only one, never waits for a person.
  void StartWorker(std::function<void(const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>& canceled)> work,
                   std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out);
  void JoinWorker();
  void StartAuthenticate(int64_t operationId, bool waitForLockScreen,
                         std::shared_ptr<common::ICancellationSignal>* out);
  void Enroll();
  void Authenticate(int64_t operationId, const std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>& canceled);
  void Save();  // mState to persist.wsa.fingerprint.u<user> (call with mLock held)

  const int32_t mUserId;
  const std::shared_ptr<ISessionCallback> mCb;

  std::mutex mLock;
  UserState mState;
  std::thread mWorker;
  std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>> mWorkerCanceled;  // the running operation's cancellation flag
  // The running authentication waits for the lock screen to be shown (see WaitsForLockScreen).
  std::atomic<bool> mWaitForLockScreen{false};
};

class WsaFingerprint : public BnFingerprint {
 public:
  WsaFingerprint();

  ndk::ScopedAStatus getSensorProps(std::vector<SensorProps>* out) override;
  ndk::ScopedAStatus createSession(int32_t sensorId, int32_t userId,
                                   const std::shared_ptr<ISessionCallback>& cb,
                                   std::shared_ptr<ISession>* out) override;

};

}  // namespace aidl::android::hardware::biometrics::fingerprint::wsa
```

```cpp
/*
 * Copyright 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar

 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
 * You may obtain a copy of the License at

 *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.
 */
#define LOG_TAG "android.hardware.biometrics.fingerprint.wsa"

#include <android/binder_manager.h>
#include <android/binder_process.h>

#include "WsaFingerprint.h"
#include "log/log.h"

using ::aidl::android::hardware::biometrics::fingerprint::wsa::WsaFingerprint;

int main() {
  ALOGI("WSA Windows Hello Fingerprint HAL starting");
  ABinderProcess_setThreadPoolMaxThreadCount(0);
  auto service = ndk::SharedRefBase::make<WsaFingerprint>();
  const std::string instance = std::string() + WsaFingerprint::descriptor + "/default";
  if (AServiceManager_addService(service->asBinder().get(), instance.c_str()) != STATUS_OK) {
    ALOGE("Could not register %s", instance.c_str());
    return 1;
  }
  ABinderProcess_joinThreadPool();
  return 0;
}
```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/fstab.1.windows`:

```windows
# Legacy WSA disk layout with file-based encryption (androidboot.fstab_suffix=1.windows).
# First-stage init reads this copy from /system/etc before /vendor is mounted.
# No /cache entry: WSA 2407 (Android 13) mounted tmpfs on a /cache directory, but in Android 15
# without a cache partition /cache is a symlink to /data/cache. On the first boot /data/cache does
# not exist yet, so that mount failed, mount_all returned an error, "nonencrypted" was never
# triggered and class main (installd) did not start: the system server stopped at every first boot.
# <src>           <mnt_point>             <type>    <mnt_flags and options>                    <fs_mgr_flags>
SCSI=0:0:0:1      /vendor                 ext4      noatime,ro,errors=panic                    wait,first_stage_mount
SCSI=0:0:0:2      /system_ext             ext4      noatime,ro,errors=panic                    wait,first_stage_mount
SCSI=0:0:0:3      /product                ext4      noatime,ro,errors=panic                    wait,first_stage_mount
SCSI=0:0:0:4      /data                   ext4      nodev,noatime,nosuid,discard,errors=panic  latemount,wait,check,quota,formattable,fileencryption=aes-256-xts,checkpoint=block
SCSI=0:0:0:5      /metadata               ext4      nodev,noatime,nosuid,errors=panic          first_stage_mount,wait,check,formattable,nofail
shared_mem        /mnt/shared_mem         virtiofs  nosuid,nodev,noatime,context=u:object_r:system_server_tmpfs:s0,dax defaults
shared_tmp        /mnt/shared_tmp         virtiofs  nosuid,nodev,noatime,context=u:object_r:media_rw_data_file:s0 defaults
shared_anr        /data/anr               virtiofs  nosuid,nodev,noatime,context=u:object_r:anr_data_file:s0 defaults
shared_tombstone  /data/tombstones        virtiofs  nosuid,nodev,noatime,context=u:object_r:tombstone_data_file:s0 defaults
```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/init/init.wsa-next.rc`:

```rc
# WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
#
# Debuggable builds start a shell on the serial console (system/core/rootdir/init.rc), and
# ActivityManager then posts "Serial console enabled - performance is impacted", which WSA shows
# as a Windows notification after every start. On WSA nobody sits at that console (adb and the
# elevator are the ways in), so it is stopped right after init.rc starts it: same trigger,
# parsed later, so this action runs second.
on init && property:ro.debuggable=1
    stop console
```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/ndk_translation/ndk_translation.rc`:

```rc
# WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
# ARM64 programs run through Google's ndk_translation; 32-bit ARM programs keep WSA's Houdini.
# The vendor init script registers Houdini for both from a property trigger; replace its
# ARM64 entries at boot, after all property triggers have run.
on boot && property:ro.enable.native.bridge.exec=1 && property:ro.dalvik.vm.isa.arm64=x86_64
    write /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/arm64_exe -1
    write /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/arm64_dyn -1
    copy /system/etc/binfmt_misc/arm64_exe /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/register
    copy /system/etc/binfmt_misc/arm64_dyn /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/register
```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/registration/src/org/wsanext/registration/ActionReceiver.java`:

```java
/*
 * Copyright 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
 *
 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
 * You may obtain a copy of the License at
 *
 *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.
 */
package org.wsanext.registration;

import android.content.BroadcastReceiver;
import android.content.ClipData;
import android.content.ClipboardManager;
import android.content.Context;
import android.content.Intent;
import android.net.Uri;
import android.widget.Toast;

/** The notification's buttons (where Android's notification is shown): copy the ID, open the page, or done. */
public final class ActionReceiver extends BroadcastReceiver {
    @Override
    public void onReceive(Context context, Intent intent) {
        final String id = intent.getStringExtra(Registration.EXTRA_ID);
        if (id == null) return;
        final String action = intent.getAction();
        if (Registration.ACTION_COPY.equals(action)) {
            context.getSystemService(ClipboardManager.class).setPrimaryClip(ClipData.newPlainText(context.getString(R.string.clip_label), id));
            Toast.makeText(context, R.string.copied, Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show();
        } else if (Registration.ACTION_OPEN.equals(action)) {
            context.startActivity(new Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse(Registration.PAGE)).addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK));
        } else if (Registration.ACTION_DONE.equals(action)) {
            Registration.done(context, id);
        }
    }
}

```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/registration/src/org/wsanext/registration/Registration.java`:

```java
/*
 * Copyright 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
 *
 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
 * You may obtain a copy of the License at
 *
 *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.
 */
package org.wsanext.registration;

import android.app.Notification;
import android.app.NotificationChannel;
import android.app.NotificationManager;
import android.app.PendingIntent;
import android.content.Context;
import android.content.Intent;
import android.content.SharedPreferences;
import android.database.Cursor;
import android.graphics.drawable.Icon;
import android.net.LocalSocket;
import android.net.LocalSocketAddress;
import android.net.Uri;
import android.util.Log;

import java.io.DataInputStream;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

/**
 * The one notification: "register this device with Google Play", with the device's Google
 * Services Framework ID. Shown once Play services have the ID, again after every start until
 * the user presses "Done" for that ID (a new installation gets a new ID and a new notification).
 */
final class Registration {
    static final String ACTION_OPEN = "org.wsanext.registration.OPEN";
    static final String ACTION_COPY = "org.wsanext.registration.COPY";
    static final String ACTION_DONE = "org.wsanext.registration.DONE";
    static final String EXTRA_ID = "id";
    static final String PAGE = "https://www.google.com/android/uncertified";

    private static final String CHANNEL = "registration";
    private static final int NOTIFICATION = 1;
    private static final Uri GSERVICES = Uri.parse("content://com.google.android.gsf.gservices");
    private static final String PREFS = "registration";
    private static final String KEY_DONE = "done_for";
    private static final String TAG = "WsaNextRegistration";
    private static final String ELEVATE_SOCKET = "/dev/socket/wsa_elevate";

    private Registration() {}

    /** The ID as Google's page asks for it (decimal), or null before Play services checked in. */
    static String gsfId(Context context) {
        final String fromProvider = gsfIdFromProvider(context);
        return fromProvider != null ? fromProvider : gsfIdFromSystem();
    }

    // Play services before 26.x answer every app holding READ_GSERVICES; current ones only
    // Google-signed apps (they log "is not approved to access the device ID" and leave it out).
    private static String gsfIdFromProvider(Context context) {
        try (Cursor cursor = context.getContentResolver().query(GSERVICES, null, null, new String[] {"android_id"}, null)) {
            if (cursor == null || !cursor.moveToFirst() || cursor.getColumnCount() < 2) return null;
            final String value = cursor.getString(1);
            if (value == null || Long.parseLong(value) == 0) return null;
            return value;
        } catch (RuntimeException e) {  // no Play services, or not a number yet
            return null;
        }
    }

    // WSA-Next's wsa-elevated hands the ID to this app only (elevate/protocol.h: "GFID").
    private static String gsfIdFromSystem() {
        try (LocalSocket socket = new LocalSocket()) {
            socket.connect(new LocalSocketAddress(ELEVATE_SOCKET, LocalSocketAddress.Namespace.FILESYSTEM));
            final OutputStream out = socket.getOutputStream();
            out.write(new byte[] {'G', 'F', 'I', 'D'});
            out.flush();
            final DataInputStream in = new DataInputStream(socket.getInputStream());
            if (in.readUnsignedByte() != 'G') return null;  // refused, or not checked in yet
            final byte[] id = new byte[in.readUnsignedByte()];
            in.readFully(id);
            final String text = new String(id, StandardCharsets.US_ASCII);
            return Long.parseLong(text) == 0 ? null : text;
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException e) {  // no wsa-elevated (not a debuggable build)
            Log.w(TAG, "No device ID from wsa-elevated: " + e);
            return null;
        }
    }

    // A click on this app's notification does not come back to Android on WSA (it has no
    // launcher activity, so Windows cannot hand the click over). WSA-Next on Windows shows the
    // notice itself: wsa-elevated reads the ID and hands it to the host (elevate/protocol.h,
    // "RGWN"), whose notification copies it and opens the page in the Windows browser. The
    // answer: 'S' shown there, 'O' registered from Windows before, anything else - not shown.
    private static int offerOnWindows() {
        try (LocalSocket socket = new LocalSocket()) {
            socket.connect(new LocalSocketAddress(ELEVATE_SOCKET, LocalSocketAddress.Namespace.FILESYSTEM));
            final OutputStream out = socket.getOutputStream();
            out.write(new byte[] {'R', 'G', 'W', 'N'});
            out.flush();
            return new DataInputStream(socket.getInputStream()).readUnsignedByte();
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException e) {  // no wsa-elevated (not a debuggable build)
            Log.w(TAG, "No notice on Windows: " + e);
            return -1;
        }
    }

    /** Offers the registration when there is an ID the user has not marked as done. */
    static void update(Context context) {
        final String id = gsfId(context);
        if (id == null) return;  // CHECKIN_COMPLETE brings us back once there is one
        if (id.equals(prefs(context).getString(KEY_DONE, null))) return;
        switch (offerOnWindows()) {
            case 'S':  // Windows shows it
                context.getSystemService(NotificationManager.class).cancel(NOTIFICATION);
                break;
            case 'O':  // registered from Windows before
                done(context, id);
                break;
            default:  // no WSA-Next host, or no icon there: Android's own notification
                show(context, id);
                break;
        }
    }

    static void done(Context context, String id) {
        prefs(context).edit().putString(KEY_DONE, id).apply();
        context.getSystemService(NotificationManager.class).cancel(NOTIFICATION);
    }

    private static SharedPreferences prefs(Context context) {
        return context.createDeviceProtectedStorageContext().getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE);
    }

    private static void show(Context context, String id) {
        final NotificationManager manager = context.getSystemService(NotificationManager.class);
        manager.createNotificationChannel(
                new NotificationChannel(CHANNEL, context.getString(R.string.channel), NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT));
        final PendingIntent open = button(context, ACTION_OPEN, id, 0);
        final Notification notification = new Notification.Builder(context, CHANNEL)
                .setSmallIcon(android.R.drawable.ic_dialog_info)
                .setContentTitle(context.getString(R.string.title))
                .setContentText(context.getString(R.string.text, id))
                .setStyle(new Notification.BigTextStyle().bigText(context.getString(R.string.text_long, id)))
                .setContentIntent(open)
                .setOnlyAlertOnce(true)
                .addAction(action(context, R.string.copy, button(context, ACTION_COPY, id, 1)))
                .addAction(action(context, R.string.open, open))
                .addAction(action(context, R.string.done, button(context, ACTION_DONE, id, 2)))
                .build();
        manager.notify(NOTIFICATION, notification);
    }

    private static PendingIntent button(Context context, String action, String id, int request) {
        final Intent intent = new Intent(action).setClass(context, ActionReceiver.class).putExtra(EXTRA_ID, id);
        return PendingIntent.getBroadcast(context, request, intent, PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE | PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT);
    }

    private static Notification.Action action(Context context, int label, PendingIntent intent) {
        return new Notification.Action.Builder(Icon.createWithResource(context, android.R.drawable.ic_menu_info_details),
                context.getString(label), intent).build();
    }
}
```

```java
/*
 * Copyright 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
 *
 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
 * You may obtain a copy of the License at
 *
 *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 *
 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
 * limitations under the License.
 */
package org.wsanext.registration;

import android.content.BroadcastReceiver;
import android.content.Context;
import android.content.Intent;

/**
 * Android has started, or Play services have checked in with Google (which is when a new
 * installation gets its ID). Anyone may send these; the receiver only looks the ID up again.
 */
public final class TriggerReceiver extends BroadcastReceiver {
    @Override
    public void onReceive(Context context, Intent intent) {
        final PendingResult pending = goAsync();  // the provider query must not hold the main thread
        new Thread(() -> {
            try {
                Registration.update(context);
            } finally {
                pending.finish();
            }
        }, "WsaNextRegistration").start();
    }
}
```

```te
# Bluetooth HCI HAL of WSA (device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/bluetooth): a platform process that serves
# android.hardware.bluetooth.IBluetoothHci/default and forwards HCI packets to the Bluetooth
# bridge on the Windows host over a Hyper-V socket (vsock).

binder_use(hal_bluetooth_wsa)
```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/sepolicy/system_ext/private/wsa_elevate.te`:

```te
# WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
#
# Root for apps, confirmed on Windows with Windows Hello (device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/elevate).
#
# wsa_elevated - the daemon: root, but a narrow domain. It talks to the Windows host over vsock,
# hears apps on /dev/socket/wsa_elevate, reads packages.list to name them, and starts
# wsa-elevate-exec, whose executable enters su - the domain AOSP keeps for root on debug
# builds, which every other domain already lets pass descriptors, binder calls and pipes to
# (pm, am, cmd work from a root shell). The daemon never receives an app's descriptors: the
# elevated process takes them from the app itself (pidfd_getfd).
type wsa_elevated, domain, coredomain, mlstrustedsubject;
type wsa_elevated_exec, system_file_type, exec_type, file_type;
type wsa_elevate_exec, system_file_type, exec_type, file_type;
type wsa_elevate_socket, file_type, coredomain_socket, mlstrustedobject;

init_daemon_domain(wsa_elevated)

# The elevation bridge on Windows connects to the daemon (vsock port "WSEV").
allow wsa_elevated self:vsock_socket { create bind listen accept read write getattr getopt setopt shutdown };

# Apps ask on the socket init creates; who they are comes from the kernel (SO_PEERCRED).
allow wsa_elevated self:unix_stream_socket { accept listen read write getattr getopt shutdown };
allow wsa_elevated packages_list_file:file r_file_perms;
allow wsa_elevated system_data_file:dir search;

# Apps and the adb shell may ask; Windows Hello decides.
unix_socket_connect({ untrusted_app_all platform_app priv_app system_app shell }, wsa_elevate, wsa_elevated)

# /dev/wsa/bin, last on the PATH: the su link for root apps while WSA-Next on Windows wants it.
type wsa_elevate_dir, file_type, mlstrustedobject;
allow wsa_elevated wsa_elevate_dir:dir { search getattr write add_name remove_name };
allow wsa_elevated wsa_elevate_dir:lnk_file { create unlink getattr };
allow { appdomain shell -isolated_app_all -sdk_sandbox_all } wsa_elevate_dir:dir { search getattr };
allow { appdomain shell -isolated_app_all -sdk_sandbox_all } wsa_elevate_dir:lnk_file { read getattr };
dontaudit domain wsa_elevate_dir:dir search;  # a command looked up on the PATH by anyone else

userdebug_or_eng(`
  # The elevated process: the executable of the launcher enters su (no apostrophes in m4 quotes).
  domain_auto_trans(wsa_elevated, wsa_elevate_exec, su)
  # Signals of the client, and a hangup when it goes away, reach the process group of the command.
  allow wsa_elevated su:process { signal sigkill sigstop };
')

```

```bp
// WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
// SIM, network and SMS for Android from the PC's modem. Android runs Cuttlefish's AT-command RIL
// as a platform HAL that listens on a Hyper-V socket (android/patches/device/google/cuttlefish);
// on Windows, WSA-Next's modem bridge (src/telephony) connects to it and answers the AT commands
// with the Windows mobile broadband API. No calls and no mobile data: the PC has its own network,
// and a laptop's modem has no voice path.

    default_applicable_licenses: ["Android-Apache-2.0"],

    name: "wsa-ril.rc",
    src: "wsa-ril.rc",
    sub_dir: "init",

    filename_from_src: true,
    sub_dir: "vintf/manifest",
    system_ext_specific: true,

// MMS: joins MmsService's connection with WSA-Next's (vsock port "WSMM"); Windows opens the

    name: "wsa-mms",
    system_ext_specific: true,
    init_rc: ["wsa-mms.rc"],
    srcs: ["wsa-mms.cpp"],
    cflags: [
        "-Wall",
        "-Wextra",
        "-Werror",
    ],
    shared_libs: [
        "libcutils",
        "liblog",
    ],
}

prebuilt_etc {
```

`android/device/wsa/wsa_x86_64/telephony/wsa-mms.cpp`:

```cpp
// WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
// MMS through the PC's modem. Android has no cellular network here: MmsService (patched,
// android/patches/packages/services/Mms) connects to /dev/socket/wsa_mms, and WSA-Next on Windows
// keeps a connection open on vsock port "WSMM". This daemon joins one of each and passes the
// bytes through unchanged: MmsService names the APN and the server in the first line, Windows
// opens that APN on the modem, connects and answers "OK", then the HTTP exchange follows.
//
// One exchange at a time: Windows opens its next connection when one ends, and a second
// MmsService connection waits in the listen queue meanwhile. Nothing polls: the daemon blocks
// in accept and poll until a side acts.

#define LOG_TAG "wsa-mms"

#include <cutils/sockets.h>
#include <linux/vm_sockets.h>
#include <log/log.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <cerrno>
#include <cstdint>

namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kBridgePort = 0x57534D4D;  // "WSMM"

int ListenForHost() {
  const int s = socket(AF_VSOCK, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC, 0);
  if (s < 0) return -1;
  sockaddr_vm address{};
  address.svm_family = AF_VSOCK;
  address.svm_port = kBridgePort;
  address.svm_cid = VMADDR_CID_ANY;
  if (bind(s, reinterpret_cast<sockaddr*>(&address), sizeof address) != 0 || listen(s, 1) != 0) {
    close(s);
    return -1;
  }
  return s;
}

bool WriteAll(int fd, const char* data, size_t size) {
  while (size > 0) {
    const ssize_t n = write(fd, data, size);
    if (n < 0 && errno == EINTR) continue;
    if (n <= 0) return false;
    data += n;
    size -= static_cast<size_t>(n);
  }
  return true;
}

// Copies both ways until both directions have ended (a side's end of data is passed on as a
// half-close) or a side fails.
void Join(int a, int b) {
  const int peer[2] = {b, a};
  pollfd fds[2] = {{a, POLLIN, 0}, {b, POLLIN, 0}};
  char buffer[16 * 1024];
  int open = 2;
  while (open > 0) {
    if (poll(fds, 2, -1) < 0) {
      if (errno == EINTR) continue;
      return;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
      if (fds[i].fd < 0 || !(fds[i].revents & (POLLIN | POLLHUP | POLLERR))) continue;
      const ssize_t n = read(fds[i].fd, buffer, sizeof buffer);
      if (n < 0 && errno == EINTR) continue;
      if (n < 0) return;
      if (n == 0) {
        shutdown(peer[i], SHUT_WR);
        fds[i].fd = -1;  // poll skips it
        --open;
        continue;
      }
      if (!WriteAll(peer[i], buffer, static_cast<size_t>(n))) return;
    }
  }
}

}  // namespace

int main() {
  const int local = android_get_control_socket("wsa_mms");
  if (local < 0 || listen(local, 4) != 0) {
    ALOGE("wsa-mms: no socket from init");
    return 1;
  }
  const int listener = ListenForHost();
  if (listener < 0) {
    ALOGE("wsa-mms: cannot listen on vsock port 0x%08X (errno %d)", kBridgePort, errno);
    return 1;
  }
  for (;;) {
    const int host = accept4(listener, nullptr, nullptr, SOCK_CLOEXEC);
    if (host < 0) continue;  // EINTR, or a connection that went away before it was taken
    // Wait for MmsService. The host speaks only after it: anything from the host now is its
    // end (WSA-Next stopped), and the next connection is taken.
    pollfd fds[2] = {{host, POLLIN, 0}, {local, POLLIN, 0}};
    for (;;) {
      if (poll(fds, 2, -1) < 0) {
        if (errno == EINTR) continue;
        break;
      }
      if (fds[0].revents) break;
      if (fds[1].revents & POLLIN) {
        const int client = accept4(local, nullptr, nullptr, SOCK_CLOEXEC);
        if (client < 0) continue;
        Join(client, host);
        close(client);
        break;
      }
    }
    close(host);
  }
}
```

`android/patches/art/0002-nativeloader-permit-the-folder-of-a-system-app.patch`:

```patch
nativeloader: let an app on a system partition load its own libraries from class loaders it makes.

A class loader that an app creates itself (not through ApplicationLoaders) gets an isolated
namespace that may load anything under /data and /mnt/expand, so that apps with custom class
loaders can load their own libraries by absolute path (b/27588281). An app on a read-only system
partition keeps its libraries in its folder there instead. Chrome makes the class loaders of its
isolated splits itself; integrated into the image (/product/app/ChromePlay) it crashed at start:
"library .../ChromePlay.apk!/lib/x86_64/libelements.so ... is not accessible for the namespace"
(permitted_paths="/data:/mnt/expand"), while its base loaded libchrome.so from the same APK. The
namespace of such a class loader now also permits the folder of the calling APK when that is an
app folder on a system partition - the app's own files and nothing else.

+std::optional<std::string> SystemAppDir(const char* location) {
+  if (location == nullptr) {
+    return std::nullopt;
+  }
+  static const std::regex kAppApk("^(/(system|system_ext|product)/(app|priv-app)/[^/]+)/[^/]+\\.apk$");
+  std::cmatch match;
+  if (!std::regex_match(location, match, kAppApk)) {
+    return std::nullopt;
+  }
```

`android/patches/device/google/cuttlefish/0002-RIL-refuse-data-calls-without-retries.patch`:

```patch
From: WSA-Next <dev@kvc.pl>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:50:00 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] RIL: refuse data calls without retries

With the host modem (-L) there is no mobile data: the PC has its own network and
MMS go through the host. requestSetupDataCall failed on the missing radio
interface with a generic error, which libril passes on with a suggested retry
time of 0, so Android retried every few milliseconds and its network stack ran
out of receivers (more than 1000 network monitors within a minute). Answer at
once with "service option not supported", a permanent failure Android does not
retry, and no suggested retry time.

+         * A permanent failure, which Android does not retry: the generic error below came back
+         * to it as "retry at once", and it retried every few milliseconds. */

+    }
```

```patch
   }
 }
 
+// Guest code run through a native bridge cannot install working seccomp filters: its
+// filters check the guest architecture and guest system call numbers, but the kernel sees
+// the host's system calls, so the first call after installation kills the process
+// (Chromium's renderer sandbox does this). Make seccomp(2) and prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP) fail
+// in such processes, as on a kernel without seccomp, so guest sandboxes skip that layer.
+// The filters installed by SetUpSeccompFilter() stay in force.
+static void BlockSeccompForNativeBridge() {
+#if defined(__x86_64__)
+  constexpr uint32_t kAuditArch = AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64;
+#elif defined(__i386__)
+  constexpr uint32_t kAuditArch = AUDIT_ARCH_I386;
+#elif defined(__aarch64__)
+  constexpr uint32_t kAuditArch = AUDIT_ARCH_AARCH64;
+#elif defined(__arm__)
+  constexpr uint32_t kAuditArch = AUDIT_ARCH_ARM;
+#elif defined(__riscv)
+  constexpr uint32_t kAuditArch = AUDIT_ARCH_RISCV64;
+#endif
+  struct sock_filter filter[] = {
+      BPF_STMT(BPF_LD | BPF_W | BPF_ABS, offsetof(struct seccomp_data, arch)),
+      BPF_JUMP(BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, kAuditArch, 0, 6),
+      BPF_STMT(BPF_LD | BPF_W | BPF_ABS, offsetof(struct seccomp_data, nr)),
+      BPF_JUMP(BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, __NR_seccomp, 5, 0),
+      BPF_JUMP(BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, __NR_prctl, 0, 3),
+      BPF_STMT(BPF_LD | BPF_W | BPF_ABS, offsetof(struct seccomp_data, args[0])),
+      BPF_JUMP(BPF_JMP | BPF_JEQ | BPF_K, PR_SET_SECCOMP, 2, 0),
```

```patch
TelephonyProvider updates its APN database from apns-conf.xml only when ro.build.id
changes. WSA-Next releases of one Android version keep AOSP's build id and differ in
the build number (and so in the fingerprint), so an update never reloaded the list:
```

```patch
+/*
+ * WSA-Next © 2026 Marek Wesołowski - wesmar
+ *
+ * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+ * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+ * You may obtain a copy of the License at
+ *
+ *      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+ *
+ * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+ * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+ * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+ * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+ * limitations under the License.
+ */
+
+package com.android.mms.service;
+
+import android.net.LocalSocket;
+import android.net.LocalSocketAddress;
+
+import java.io.Closeable;
+import java.io.File;
+import java.io.IOException;
+import java.io.InputStream;
+import java.io.OutputStream;
+import java.net.HttpURLConnection;
+import java.net.InetAddress;
+import java.net.InetSocketAddress;
+import java.net.Proxy;
+import java.net.ServerSocket;
+import java.net.Socket;
+import java.net.URL;
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
+
+/**
+ * WSA-Next (Windows Subsystem for Android): the SIM is in the PC's modem, which Windows drives,
+ * and Android has no cellular network of its own. MMS go this way instead:
+ *
+ * <pre>
+ *   MmsHttpClient -> loopback tunnel (here) -> /dev/socket/wsa_mms (the wsa-mms daemon)
+ *     -> vsock -> WSA-Next on Windows: opens the APN on the modem and connects to the server
+ * </pre>
+ *
+ * The tunnel's first line names the APN and the server (the APN's MMS proxy, or the MMS server
+ * itself); Windows answers "OK" once connected, then the bytes go through unchanged. One tunnel
+ * carries one HTTP exchange.
+ */
+final class WsaMmsRelay {
+    /** The net ID MmsNetworkManager reports: there is no Android network. */
+    static final int NET_ID = 0;
+
+    private static final String SOCKET_NAME = "wsa_mms";
+    private static final File SOCKET_FILE = new File("/dev/socket/" + SOCKET_NAME);
+    // A guard: Windows answers as soon as the APN is up and the server took the connection.
+    private static final int ANSWER_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 * 1000;
+    private static final int MAX_LINE = 1024;
+
+    private WsaMmsRelay() {}
+
+    /** True on WSA-Next, whose relay daemon owns the socket. */
+    static boolean isAvailable() {
+        return SOCKET_FILE.exists();
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Asks the host for a connection to the APN's MMS proxy (when set) or to the server of `url`,
+     * through the APN.
+     */
+    static Tunnel open(ApnSettings apn, URL url, boolean isProxySet, String proxyHost,
+            int proxyPort, String requestId) throws IOException {
+        final boolean https = "https".equalsIgnoreCase(url.getProtocol());
+        final String host = isProxySet ? proxyHost : url.getHost();
+        final int port = isProxySet ? proxyPort
+                : (url.getPort() != -1 ? url.getPort() : url.getDefaultPort());
+        final LocalSocket relay = new LocalSocket();
+        try {
+            relay.connect(new LocalSocketAddress(SOCKET_NAME,
+                    LocalSocketAddress.Namespace.RESERVED));
+            relay.setSoTimeout(ANSWER_TIMEOUT_MS);
+            final String request = "MMS\t" + field(apn.getApn()) + '\t' + apn.getAuthType()
+                    + '\t' + field(apn.getUser()) + '\t' + field(apn.getPassword())
+                    + '\t' + field(host) + '\t' + port + '\n';
+            relay.getOutputStream().write(request.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
+            final String answer = readLine(relay.getInputStream());
+            if (!"OK".equals(answer)) {
+                throw new IOException("WSA-Next host: " + answer);
+            }
+            relay.setSoTimeout(0);
+            LogUtil.i(requestId, "HTTP: through the WSA-Next host, APN " + apn.getApn());
+            return new Tunnel(relay, https && !isProxySet, isProxySet || https);
+        } catch (IOException e) {
+            closeQuietly(relay);
+            throw e;
+        }
+    }
+
+    /** One HTTP exchange through the host: a loopback listener for a single connection. */
+    static final class Tunnel implements Closeable {
+        private final LocalSocket mRelay;
+        private final ServerSocket mServer;
+        // https straight to the server: the client's CONNECT is answered here (the host has
+        // already connected to the server).
+        private final boolean mAnswerConnect;
+        // The loopback end acts as the client's HTTP proxy (an MMS proxy, or https).
+        private final boolean mAsProxy;
+        private volatile Socket mClient;
+
+        Tunnel(LocalSocket relay, boolean answerConnect, boolean asProxy) throws IOException {
+            mRelay = relay;
+            mAnswerConnect = answerConnect;
+            mAsProxy = asProxy;
+            mServer = new ServerSocket(0, 1, InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress());
+            final Thread thread = new Thread(this::serve, "WsaMmsRelay");
+            thread.setDaemon(true);
+            thread.start();
+        }
+
+        HttpURLConnection openConnection(URL url) throws IOException {
+            final InetSocketAddress local =
+                    new InetSocketAddress(InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress(), mServer.getLocalPort());
+            if (mAsProxy) {
+                return (HttpURLConnection) url.openConnection(new Proxy(Proxy.Type.HTTP, local));
+            }
+            // Straight to the MMS server: the loopback end in the URL, the server's name in Host.
+            final URL direct = new URL("http", local.getAddress().getHostAddress(),
+                    local.getPort(), url.getFile());
+            final HttpURLConnection connection =
+                    (HttpURLConnection) direct.openConnection(Proxy.NO_PROXY);
+            connection.setRequestProperty("Host",
+                    url.getPort() != -1 ? url.getHost() + ":" + url.getPort() : url.getHost());
+            return connection;
+        }
+
+        private void serve() {
+            try (Socket client = mServer.accept()) {
+                mClient = client;
+                closeQuietly(mServer);
+                final InputStream fromClient = client.getInputStream();
+                final OutputStream toClient = client.getOutputStream();
+                if (mAnswerConnect) {
+                    skipHeader(fromClient);
+                    toClient.write("HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\r\n\r\n"
+                            .getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII));
+                    toClient.flush();
+                }
+                final Thread upstream = new Thread(() -> {
+                    try {
+                        copy(fromClient, mRelay.getOutputStream());
+                        mRelay.shutdownOutput();
+                    } catch (IOException e) {
+                        // The tunnel ends
+                    }
+                }, "WsaMmsRelay-up");
+                upstream.setDaemon(true);
+                upstream.start();
+                copy(mRelay.getInputStream(), toClient);
+                client.shutdownOutput();
+                upstream.join();
+            } catch (IOException | InterruptedException e) {
+                // close(), or a side went away
+            } finally {
+                close();
+            }
+        }
+
+        @Override
+        public void close() {
+            closeQuietly(mServer);
+            closeQuietly(mClient);
+            closeQuietly(mRelay);
+        }
+    }
+
+    private static String field(String value) {
+        return value == null ? "" : value.replace('\t', ' ').replace('\r', ' ').replace('\n', ' ');
+    }
+
+    private static String readLine(InputStream in) throws IOException {
+        final StringBuilder line = new StringBuilder();
+        for (;;) {
+            final int c = in.read();
+            if (c < 0) {
+                throw new IOException("WSA-Next host gave no answer");
+            }
+            if (c == '\n') {
+                return line.toString();
+            }
+            if (line.length() >= MAX_LINE) {
+                throw new IOException("WSA-Next host: answer too long");
+            }
+            line.append((char) c);
+        }
+    }
+
+    // The header of the client's CONNECT request, up to the empty line.
+    private static void skipHeader(InputStream in) throws IOException {
+        int matched = 0;  // of "\r\n\r\n"
+        for (int count = 0; matched < 4; ++count) {
+            final int c = in.read();
+            if (c < 0 || count > 16 * 1024) {
+                throw new IOException("no CONNECT request");
+            }
+            matched = (c == '\r' && (matched == 0 || matched == 2)) ? matched + 1
+                    : (c == '\n' && (matched == 1 || matched == 3)) ? matched + 1
+                    : (c == '\r') ? 1 : 0;
+        }
+    }
+
+    private static void copy(InputStream in, OutputStream out) throws IOException {
+        final byte[] buffer = new byte[16 * 1024];
+        int count;
+        while ((count = in.read(buffer)) > 0) {
+            out.write(buffer, 0, count);
+            out.flush();
+        }
+    }
+
+    private static void closeQuietly(Closeable closeable) {
+        if (closeable == null) {
+            return;
+        }
+        try {
+            closeable.close();
+        } catch (IOException e) {
+            // Already closed
+        }
+    }
+}
```

```patch
+// Windows Subsystem for Android names its disks in the fstab by SCSI address
+// ("SCSI=<host>:<channel>:<target>:<lun>"): the address is stable across boots while
+// the sdX enumeration order is not. Resolve such entries through sysfs to the block node.
+static void ResolveScsiAddress(std::string* blk_device) {
+    static constexpr char kPrefix[] = "SCSI=";
+    if (!android::base::StartsWith(*blk_device, kPrefix)) {
+        return;
+    }
+    const std::string address = blk_device->substr(sizeof(kPrefix) - 1);
+    const std::string block_dir = "/sys/bus/scsi/devices/" + address + "/block";
+    std::unique_ptr<DIR, decltype(&closedir)> dir(opendir(block_dir.c_str()), closedir);
+    if (!dir) {
+        PERROR << "Failed to resolve SCSI address " << address;
+        return;
+    }
+    while (const struct dirent* entry = readdir(dir.get())) {
+        if (entry->d_name[0] == '.') {
+            continue;
+        }
+        *blk_device = std::string("/dev/block/") + entry->d_name;
+        LINFO << "Resolved SCSI address " << address << " to " << *blk_device;
+        return;
+    }
+    LERROR << "Failed to resolve SCSI address " << address << ": no block device";
+}
```
